items.title: UNN PANS dismisses reports of seven students’ deaths
items.description: By Alumona Ukwueze The Pharmaceutical Association of Nigerian Students (PANS), University of Nigeria, Nsukka (UNN) chapter, has dismissed reports that seven pharmacy students died in a party-related incident at End in Praise Lodge, Hilltop, Nsukka, Enugu State. The association said there was no confirmed evidence that any pharmacy student was among those who died in the incident, urging the public to stop circulating unverified information. The clarification was contained in a statement dated November 12, 2026, jointly signed by the association’s President, Comr. Onah Olisaemeka A., and Secretary-General, Comr. Obasi Chibuike V. PANS said it was reacting to reports circulating on social media alleging that seven pharmacy students lost their lives in the incident. According to the statement, the association’s president personally visited Faith Foundation Hospital, where the bodies of four victims, comprising two males and two females, were deposited at the mortuary. He said he also viewed the bodies but did not recognise any of the deceased as pharmacy students. The president further disclosed that he made enquiries about the victims and other persons affected by the incident, noting that two familiar UNN social media personalities were among those hospitalised. They were identified as Rumez, known for street vlogging, and Golden, who is popular for dance-related content. Expressing concern over the anxiety generated by the reports among pharmacy students, their families and the wider university community, the association urged the public to exercise restraint and avoid spreading unverified information. PANS said it would continue to monitor developments and communicate any verified information relevant to its members as investigations and further enquiries progressed. The association also sympathised with everyone affected by the incident and prayed for the victims and their families. items.title: Jensen Huang steps down as Nvidia CEO after reports of extramarital affairs
items.description: Jensen Huang resigned as chief executive of Nvidia on Thursday, ending his 33-year run at the helm of the AI giant he co-founded after revelations that he had two extramarital affairs, including with a woman accused of spying for China. The company’s board said Huang had stepped down as president, chief executive and board member, effective immediately. Chief financial officer Colette Kress will serve as interim CEO while keeping her finance role, and the board will consider internal and external candidates for a permanent replacement. It named former Synopsys CEO and board member Harvey Jones as its first-ever board chairman. Meanwhile, US President Donald Trump said that former Apple CEO Tim Cook should replace Huang at Nvidia. “Now that Nvidia CEO JENSEN HUANG, who has done a fantastic job, has resigned, there is only one man to take his place – TIM COOK of Apple. A Legend replaces a Legend!” Trump, who was close to Huang, said on his Truth Social network. Huang, who co-founded Nvidia and is its fourth-largest investor with a stake of about 3.61 per cent, will exit the board as well. Nvidia shares fell more than 10pc in premarket trading, and weighed on the broader market. Pressure had been mounting on Huang in recent days after reports said the 63-year-old, who is married, had an affair with a Chinese businesswoman who US authorities suspect of spying for Beijing. Nvidia’s board met on Wednesday to consider his ouster, a person familiar with the matter said, after reports earlier in the day that Huang also had an extramarital affair with a senior company executive who reported to him. Huang’s exit plunges the $4 trillion company into uncertainty and threatens to disrupt an AI ecosystem that he helped bankroll by pouring Nvidia’s swelling cash pile back into cloud providers, suppliers and the industry’s biggest labs. “The risk is not that Nvidia suddenly loses its technology roadmap … that roadmap is largely visible for the next several years. The risk is execution. Jensen has been the chief conductor of an extraordinarily complex system,” said Michael Feldman, portfolio manager at ClearBridge Investments. “In a world with real bottlenecks, that coordination is a competitive advantage in itself.” Investor sentiment toward AI stocks has already been shaky as soaring cash burn and rising debt at traditionally cash-rich tech giants fuel doubts over whether the AI boom will pay off. The departure could also have far-reaching consequences for US chip export policy, given Huang’s push to preserve access to the Chinese market and his close ties with US President Donald Trump. Trump said on Sunday that Huang had “done an amazing job for our country” and that the Nvidia chief had told him he had no idea the Chinese woman he had an affair with was a spy. Huang’s rockstar status For years, Nvidia was best known to gamers chasing top-tier graphics. But its chips’ ability to perform many calculations at once has made them the oil of the AI boom and a strategic prize in the US-China race to dominate the technology. It also made Nvidia the world’s most valuable company. That turned Huang into a rockstar CEO, mobbed by fans in Taiwan and South Korea who ask him to sign books, posters and sometimes even their bodies. Such is his pull that stocks moved at his mere mention of company names at events. But scrutiny of his conduct has intensified in recent days after reports of his relationship with Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore-based cloud company Megaspeed, who US authorities have concluded was a Chinese intelligence asset. The two, who have been photographed together in Taiwan, Singapore and California, are not related. Washington has also investigated Megaspeed, a coveted official Nvidia cloud partner with priority access to its chips, over suspicions it helped China obtain advanced AI chips restricted under US export controls, according to media reports. Beijing has denied Alice Huang is a spy. Earlier this month, Nvidia’s board launched a probe , led by independent directors with outside legal counsel, into whether Jensen Huang had been targeted by a foreign intelligence operation. It also expressed confidence in him at the time. The controversy escalated on Wednesday when the New York Times reported Huang also had an affair with Kimberly Powell, Nvidia’s vice president of healthcare, who reported to him.

items.title: CEC Raja alleges federal govt wants to 'sabotage' Islamabad local govt polls
items.description: ISLAMABAD: Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Sikandar Sultan Raja on Thursday accused the federal government of trying to sabotage the local government elections in Islamabad, clarifying that the polls would be held as scheduled. The Election Commission of Pakistan (ECP) has scheduled the polls for Dec 20. The last LG term expired in Feb 2021, and the ECP was supposed to conduct elections within 120 days. However, the federal government and the ECP spent the last several years carrying out delimitations and announcing election schedules, only to postpone the polls later. On Thursday, a three-member bench headed by the CEC heard the case about alleged violations of the electoral code in the NA-77 by-election . During the hearing, Raja mentioned that the federal government has ordered that teachers would not be assigned duty in the Islamabad LG polls. “Where will the [ECP] bring staff from?” asked Raja, who remains the CEC by virtue of the 26th Amendment , though his constitutionally mandated five-year term ended on Jan 26, 2025. “The [ECP] issues directions to the prime minister and the government; directions do not come from them to us,” the election commissioner said. Taking notice of the Centre’s order, he claimed: “The federal government wants to sabotage the Islamabad local government elections. “I make it clear that local government elections will be held in Islamabad,” Raja clarified. During the hearing, ECP Secretary Omar Hamid recalled that a candidate of the Pakistan Markazi Muslim League (PMML) had filed an application with the district returning officer, stating that Information Minister Attaullah Tarar and Farooq Tarar had visited NA-77. Special Secretary Zafar Iqbal said the application stated that the information minister had visited the constituency and violated the code of conduct. “Attaullah Tarar can be sentenced to two years for violation of the code of conduct. The [ECP] should take strict action. MNAs and ministers holding office kept roaming in the constituency,” he said. The CEC asked where the information minister was, as he had been summoned in his personal capacity. Counsel for Tarar, Sajeel Swati, said the minister was currently on an official foreign visit, referring to him accompanying the prime minister to Turkiye . “These are serious allegations. The Commission is held in great respect,” the counsel said. CEC Raja remarked that the information minister only “had to do media coverage on the visit; what else was he to do”. The CEC then addressed PML-N MPA and office-bearer Asma Naz, saying she kept roaming inside a polling station. “Your position as MPA can go. Such tactics do not increase votes; they decrease them. You are smiling; it seems you have no remorse. A notice of contempt of the [ECP] can be issued to you,” he warned. MPA Qudsia Batool, who had also been accused of violating the election code, said she was in her car and about to leave when the video was made. The Gujranwala deputy commissioner appeared and said they had no information about Tarar’s visit to the constituency. The CEC observed that the minister had come by helicopter, so a helipad must have been prepared. “How are you a DC that you do not even know that a minister is coming?” The DC replied that the helicopter had landed in the cantonment, which was not in their jurisdiction. The CEC then said the DC did not know what his powers were in the cantonment. “Go and read the law. We have also held these offices.” Raja said a fact-finding inquiry had been conducted on the violation of the code of conduct in the by-election, a copy of which would be given to all. “You will all be given that order. You respond to the report; the commission will pass an appropriate order against you, DC. Action will be taken against all three, the DC, the [returning officer] and the [district monitoring officer].” On the request of Tarar’s counsel, the CEC said, “We give you 10 days. On the next hearing, all members will appear in person.” The hearing was then adjourned till Dec 1. ECP issues updated list of registered parties Meanwhile, the ECP issued an updated list of 160 political parties registered with it. The names of the heads of the Muttahida Qaumi Movement-Pakistan (MQM-P) and the Pashtunkhwa Milli Awami Party (PkMAP) — Khalid Maqbool Siddiqui and Mahmood Khan Achakzai — have been removed from the list. In April, the ECP had given MQM-P time till Oct 15 to hold its intra-party elections as it heard a case on the matter. A senior ECP official explained to Dawn that MQM-P had not been delisted as of yet. He said the ECP had issued a show cause notice to MQM-P over failure to hold intra-party elections, with directives to respond within 14 days. He said a reply has been received, and if it fails to satisfy the commission, the case will be fixed for hearing and the matter will be decided accordingly. The PkMAP chief’s name has also been removed, as the case of its intra-party elections and an amendment to its constitution remains pending before the ECP. PTI, which lost its bat electoral symbol in January 2024 as the Supreme Court upheld the ECP’s decision in the case of its intra-party polls, also remains registered without the name of its party head. The Pakistan Sunni Tehreek is also listed without the name of its party head. Tehreek-i-Labbaik Pakistan , which was declared a proscribed organisation a year ago, is included among registered parties, but the name of its head has been removed. The name of Awaam Pakistan, headed by former prime minister Shahid Khaqan Abbasi, which had already been delisted by the ECP, is also on the list. The list also includes Islami Jamhoori Ittehad (IJI), a nine-party alliance formed in 1988 and dissolved over 33 years ago. The list also mentions some less popular political parties, including Ittehad-i-Ummat Pakistan, Jamaat-i-Suffah, Labour Qaumi Movement, Awami Democratic Party, Pakistan Qabail Movement, and Tehreek-i-Tarraqi o Kamal, without naming their party heads.

items.title: Singer Boj shares essential items to survive Detty December in Lagos
items.description: Nigerian singer and songwriter BOJ has shared some of his essential items for navigating the Detty December festivities, advising partygoers to prepare for the heat, crowded venues and messy environments expected during the festive season. Speaking in an interview with LSTV, the singer said the December festivities would be particularly intense, urging people to come prepared. We linked up with Nigerian singer, songwriter, and creative director Boj [ @BojDRB ] for his Detty December ESSENTIALS and he spoke facts . pic.twitter.com/tskJV12t3C — LSTVWW (@lstvww) November 12, 2026 “Everywhere is going to be hot. I don’t know if you guys have of El Nino,” he said. Listing his must-have items, BOJ identified a face towel as one of the most important things to carry, noting that the heat and activities during the festive period would make it particularly useful. “First of all, you’re going to need a face towel, very key,” he said. He also recommended wearing shoes other than white, warning that partygoers would likely encounter spilled drinks, water and crowded environments at various events. “Personally, I also think that shoes that are not white because you’re going to be stepping everywhere, you’re going to be choked of water. Just always have that because it’s going to be a lot of drinking,” he added. Detty December has become a major feature of Nigeria’s end-of-year entertainment calendar, attracting Nigerians in the diaspora and international visitors for a series of concerts, parties, festivals and social events. items.title: Coopération: les experts burkinabè et gabonais en conclave dans le cadre de la 2e Commission mixte
items.description: (Libreville, le 12 novembre 2026) La 2e session de la grande Commission mixte de coopération entre le Burkina Faso et la République gabonaise, a débuté, ce mercredi 11 novembre 2026, à Libreville par la réunion des experts. Ceux-ci ont pour tâche, d'examiner les projets d'accords de coopération, qui seront par la suite signés par les ministres des Affaires étrangères des deux pays. Les projets d'accords touchent divers secteurs comme l’agriculture, la sécurité, la protection civile, le commerce, l’éducation, l’enseignement supérieur, la formation professionnelle, le travail et la protection sociale, le tourisme, la culture et le sport, entre autres. Il s’agira concrètement pour les deux délégations d’examiner dans un premier temps l’état de la coopération entre Ouagadougou et Libreville puis d’analyser les projets d’instruments juridiques, qui vont permettre de poser les bases d’un partenariat solide, selon le chef de la délégation burkinabè, le Camarade Secrétaire général du ministère des Affaires étrangères, Hermann Yirigouin TOE. « Les experts sont donc appelés à élaborer un cadre de coopération bâtit sur le développement socioéconomique durable susceptible d’améliorer le quotidien de leurs populations respectives, en tenant compte des enjeux du moment et des priorités nationales », a-t-il précisé. Pour le Chef de la délégation gabonaise, par ailleurs Secrétaire général du ministère en charge des Affaires étrangères de la République Gabonaise, l’Ambassadeur Valentin LOEMBA BAYONN, la tenue de cette session traduit la convergence de vues des deux Présidents Ibrahim TRAORÉ du Burkina Faso et Brice Clotaire OLIGUI NGUEMA du Gabon, sur les grandes questions africaines et internationales. A noter que cette session de la Commission mixte de coopération entre le Burkina Faso et la République gabonaise, intervient après la première qui a eu lieu en novembre 2012 à Ouagadougou. DCRP/MAE L’article Coopération: les experts burkinabè et gabonais en conclave dans le cadre de la 2e Commission mixte est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .

items.title: 2027 budget should ensure fiscal discipline, direct investment towards productive enterprises and jobs – Deloitte
items.description: Deloitte Ghana has called for prudent fiscal discipline for the 2027 fiscal year. This call was contained in the professional services firm’s pre-budget analysis ahead of Ghana’s 2027 budget reading. The firm believes that while real gross domestic product grew by 6.0% year-on-year in the second quarter of 2026, and inflation stood at 5.5% in October, a prudent fiscal balance will be needed to sustain economic stability. With the government’s policy theme, “New Economy, New Ghana: Jobs and Prosperity”, signalling a strategic shift towards productive investment and employment, expectations centre on translating macroeconomic stability into tangible private-sector growth. Stability and private sector growth Lower inflation provides firms with a reliable basis for pricing and investment planning. However, the document noted that “lower inflation gives businesses a firmer basis for pricing and investment planning. It does not establish stronger demand in every market”. It further urged leaders to utilise this stability in reviewing expansion projects based on real customer demand. Enterprise growth and tax administration The 2024 Integrated Business Establishment Survey revealed that nine in ten establishments are micro-enterprises, with only 7.7% classified as formal. This reinforces the need for tax administration to focus on broadening the tax base and improving compliance rather than introducing major new headline taxes. Specific cost pressures may include “higher fuel-oil levies” and “higher local beverage excise within three local-content bands”, the document added. Productive investments and fiscal discipline Deloitte further stated that “additional public investment will create lasting business value only when projects remove production bottlenecks. Funding alone is insufficient”, emphasising the call for increased fiscal discipline. Whereas the government proposes reducing the primary surplus from 1.5% to 0.5% of GDP, freeing budget room for the new economy, targeted spending will be needed to ensure maximum returns. Growth and employment With youth unemployment remaining a critical issue, public investment must support sustainable job creation. Programmes like the 24-Hour Economy and Accelerated Export Development Programme target 1.7 million jobs by the end of 2028, though remain subject to delivery. In his comments, Mr. Daniel Owusu, Country Managing Partner for Deloitte Ghana, called for improved compliance and enforcement in revenue mobilisation. On infrastructure projects, he urged the need to explore viable funding options to complete deferred projects. “Leadership teams should use the approved budget as an immediate input into their 2027 strategies, pricing, investment spending, and planning for their desired economic outcomes,” Mr. Owusu admonished businesses. Deloitte’s perspective From Deloitte’s perspective, “the 2027 Budget should protect fiscal discipline while directing investment towards productive enterprises and sustainable jobs”. Firms must link capital commitments to credible customers and reliable infrastructure to secure commercial value

items.title: Zamfara commissioner dies at 50, governor mourns
items.description: By Idris Salisu, Gusau Zamfara State Governor, Dauda Lawal, has mourned the death of the state’s Commissioner for Commerce, Tasiu Musa Shinkafi, who died on Wednesday at the age of 50. Shinkafi reportedly died in a hospital in Kaduna following a brief illness. In a condolence message, Lawal described his death as an irreparable loss to the state government, his family and the people of Zamfara. The governor said, “With heavy hearts and in total submission to the will of Almighty Allah (T), we received the shocking news of the passing of the Commissioner for Commerce, Tasiu Musa Shinkafi. “Tasiu’s death is a great loss not only to his family and the state government, but also to the people of Zamfara. “He will be remembered for his dedication, honesty, and commitment to Zamfara State.” Lawal recalled that Shinkafi had previously served as Commissioner for Youth and Sport before his redeployment to the Ministry of Commerce. Describing the deceased as a valued member of his administration and a brother in service, the governor said his contributions to governance, politics and public service would be remembered. He prayed to Almighty Allah to forgive the deceased’s shortcomings and grant his family the strength to bear the loss. The post Zamfara commissioner dies at 50, governor mourns appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Oyo SDP candidate sues INEC over omission from list
items.description: By Adeola Badru The governorship candidate of the Social Democratic Party (SDP) in Oyo State, Olusegun Agboola, has dragged the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) before the Federal High Court in Abuja over the omission of his name from the commission’s list of candidates for the 2027 governorship election. Agboola alleged that unnamed political interests were behind his exclusion, describing the development as illegal, inexplicable and politically motivated. The SDP candidate, who maintained that he had fulfilled all the necessary electoral requirements, said he was seeking a court order compelling INEC to include his name on the list. In a statement on Thursday, Agboola expressed concern over what he described as the selective omission of his name despite his qualification to contest the election. He said, “The illegal and unexplainable omission of my name from the latest INEC published list as the SDP governorship candidate for Oyo State is perplexing. “Of all qualified candidates, my name was singled out and omitted from the published list without any reason from INEC.” Agboola alleged that the omission was an attempt to weaken the SDP’s political standing ahead of the election, claiming that some politicians in rival parties were uncomfortable with the party’s agenda and positions on issues affecting the state. He said, “I have been told that some people from other popular parties are behind it. They are not comfortable with all we stand for, so they want to use INEC to diminish our campaign and suppress all our efforts.” Expressing confidence in the judicial process, the candidate said he expected the court to compel INEC to correct the omission, questioning why he had to seek legal intervention after complying with the prescribed procedures. “We have followed due process and the court will soon mandate INEC to include our names, but why is that necessary?” he queried. He further alleged that his exclusion was part of a broader attempt by unnamed political interests to manipulate the electoral process and influence the outcome of the 2027 governorship election. “Some people want to use every means possible to doctor the outcome. This is sad for our democracy and shows the integrity of the umpire is damaged if this anomaly is not loudly corrected with a very public announcement from the INEC chairman,” he added. Agboola said Oyo State needed practical and sustainable solutions to unemployment, insecurity, inadequate infrastructure and other socio-economic challenges. He argued that addressing the problems required deliberate, systemic and long-term interventions rather than temporary measures. The post Oyo SDP candidate sues INEC over omission from list appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Armed robbers steal goods worth 1mn euros in Paris jewellery heist
items.description: Armed robbers stole goods worth more than one million euros ($1.1 million) from a De Beers jewellery store in Paris Thursday before fleeing on scooters, authorities and a police source told AFP. The suspects, carrying long guns, targeted the store in the city’s 2nd arrondissement at around 11:00 am (1000 GMT). During the robbery, they brandished their weapons but did not open fire, and no one was injured, according to the Paris police. A police source estimated the value at more than one million euros, confirming an earlier report by French broadcaster Europe 1. Four suspects in balaclavas, one armed with an assault rifle, are believed to have fled on motorbikes towards the motorway, according to the same source, who spoke on condition of anonymity. The Paris police said it has deployed significant resources to track down the perpetrators. The organised crime unit has opened an investigation into “armed robbery by an organised gang”, the prosecutor’s office said. Industry giant De Beers has long dominated the trade in diamonds from southern Africa. The post Armed robbers steal goods worth 1mn euros in Paris jewellery heist appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Pollution minière à Siguiri : le Procureur de la CRIEF réclame des comptes aux autorités locales
items.description: La dégradation de l’environnement dans la préfecture de Siguiri, sous l’effet notamment des activités d’exploitation minière, continue de susciter des réactions. Le procureur spécial de la Cour de répression des infractions économiques et financières (CRIEF), Alphonse Charles Wright, a vivement interpellé les autorités administratives et les services techniques sur leur responsabilité dans cette situation. Invité exceptionnel de nos confrères de Télé 24, ce jeudi 12 novembre 2026, le magistrat a dénoncé les insuffisances dans la protection des populations et appelé à une véritable prise de responsabilité à tous les niveaux de l’administration. À Siguiri, un environnement devenu hostile aux populations Pour Alphonse Charles Wright, la dégradation environnementale dans la préfecture de Siguiri est une réalité ancienne, dont il dit avoir personnellement mesuré l'ampleur lors de déplacements sur le terrain. Une manière, selon lui, de dépasser les simples images et commentaires qui circulent sur les réseaux sociaux. Le procureur spécial décrit un environnement particulièrement difficile pour les habitants, marqué par une chaleur suffocante, une forte concentration de poussière et la pollution des cours d’eau, des fleuves et des marigots. Autant de facteurs qui, à ses yeux, exposent les populations à de graves risques sanitaires et compromettent leurs conditions de vie. « Quand vous partez à Siguiri, le premier élément du déclin climatique que vous sentez, c’est cette chaleur suffocante, la poussière, avec le développement de toutes sortes de maladies pulmonaires », a-t-il expliqué. Il s'est également inquiété de la dégradation des ressources hydriques, considérant que la pollution des cours d'eau constitue une menace directe pour les communautés. « Pas d’eau, pas de vie », a-t-il martelé, plaidant pour une action en profondeur contre les causes de cette crise environnementale. « Il faut s’attaquer au problème à la racine » Le procureur spécial a ensuite critiqué les interventions ponctuelles et les réactions de circonstance qui, selon lui, ne permettent pas de trouver des solutions durables à la situation environnementale de Siguiri. Évoquant une vidéo attribuée à un ressortissant burkinabè, dans laquelle celui-ci aurait déclaré vouloir contribuer à la destruction de l'environnement guinéen au profit du développement du Burkina Faso, Alphonse Charles Wright a invité à ne pas réduire le débat à cette seule séquence devenue virale sur les réseaux sociaux. À ses yeux, cette polémique ne doit pas occulter une réalité bien plus ancienne et profonde. La dégradation de l'environnement appelle plutôt une réponse structurelle, avec des responsabilités clairement établies et des mesures concrètes pour mettre fin aux pratiques préjudiciables aux populations et aux ressources naturelles. Préfets, sous-préfets et services techniques interpellés Au-delà du constat environnemental, Alphonse Charles Wright a particulièrement insisté sur les responsabilités des autorités administratives et des services chargés du contrôle des activités minières. Il estime que les défaillances éventuelles doivent être recherchées à tous les échelons de l'administration, des autorités locales jusqu'aux services techniques et au département en charge des Mines. Les préfets, sous-préfets, présidents de district et autres responsables locaux ne sauraient, selon cette approche, être écartés de l'examen des responsabilités liées à la surveillance des activités minières et à la protection des populations. Le magistrat a également évoqué l'existence de pratiques coutumières non écrites qui encadreraient certaines activités dans les localités concernées. Il juge nécessaire de les examiner pour mieux comprendre les rapports entre exploitants miniers, communautés riveraines et autorités locales. Il a ainsi insisté sur l'importance de confronter les différentes versions et de réunir des éléments suffisamment solides pour établir les responsabilités de chaque acteur, plutôt que de tirer des conclusions à partir de témoignages isolés. La santé des populations ne doit plus être sacrifiée Pour Alphonse Charles Wright, la protection de l'environnement et de la santé publique doit constituer une priorité absolue. Les autorités compétentes ont, selon lui, le devoir d'intervenir dès lors que les conditions de vie des citoyens sont menacées par les activités économiques et minières. Il plaide également pour une meilleure coordination entre les structures administratives, les services techniques et les autorités chargées de la réglementation minière, afin de garantir une application effective des textes en vigueur. À travers cette intervention, le procureur spécial de la CRIEF remet ainsi sur la table la question de la responsabilité collective dans la dégradation de l'environnement à Siguiri. Au-delà des exploitants miniers, son interpellation vise également les responsables administratifs et les structures de contrôle, appelés à rendre compte de leur rôle dans la préservation des ressources naturelles et la protection des populations.

items.title: Politicians deceive voters to win elections – Kukah
items.description: The Catholic Bishop of Sokoto Diocese, Matthew Kukah, has accused politicians of making unrealistic promises during election campaigns to secure votes, rather than preparing Nigerians for the realities and challenges of governance. Kukah said politicians often deploy attractive images, grand promises and appealing narratives to sell voters a vision of a better society, only to abandon their commitments after assuming office and begin offering excuses for their inability to deliver. He spoke on Thursday in Abuja at a public symposium organised by the National Institute for Legislative and Democratic Studies (NILDS) in collaboration with The Kukah Centre. To illustrate the disconnect between campaign promises and governance, Kukah narrated the story of a politician who used impressive images of tarred roads, bridges, beautiful houses and children in smart school uniforms to persuade voters during his campaign. According to him, the politician won the election, but three years later, residents complained that none of the promised projects had been executed. When confronted, the politician reportedly told them: “You are confusing campaign with governance. What I did was purely a simple campaign. Governance is a difficult part.” Kukah said the response reflected a recurring pattern in Nigeria’s political system, where politicians make ambitious promises to win elections but resort to excuses after taking office. He said, “And this is why we have Nigerian politicians turn around, once they have been sworn in and after telling us all the things they want to do, and say, ‘We didn’t know that the treasury was so empty.’ Then, they start giving one excuse after the other.” The bishop argued that politicians were often more interested in creating attractive campaign narratives than communicating the realities of governance. He, however, said voters had a responsibility to interrogate political promises and assess their feasibility rather than accept campaign messages at face value. He stated, “The point I am making is that it is the business of politicians to seduce, deceive or tell us things we can’t do just to win our votes. But we are sufficiently knowledgeable, and our experience should help us to test the limits of the claims that politicians make.” Kukah urged Nigerians to develop the capacity to question politicians, scrutinise their proposals and demand accountability, stressing that citizens should not wait until elections are over before engaging the political elite. He also called for political choices that transcend ethnic, religious and class considerations. Jega urges issue-based campaigns Earlier, former Chairman of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), Prof. Attahiru Jega, said the responsibility for addressing Nigeria’s electoral challenges should not rest solely on the electoral commission. Jega urged political parties and candidates to promote issue-based campaigns and responsible political messaging, while calling on electoral and other government institutions to communicate transparently, consistently and promptly. He said, “Political parties and candidates must promote issue-based campaigns and responsible political messaging. Electoral and other government institutions must communicate transparently, consistently and promptly. Security agencies must provide credible information while maintaining professionalism. “I encourage us to draw lessons from our previous electoral experiences, identify existing gaps and develop practical recommendations for improving political communication and safeguarding election security ahead of the 2027 elections.” Jega commended NILDS and The Kukah Centre for organising the symposium, expressing hope that its discussions would strengthen public confidence, promote peaceful political competition and contribute to a sustainable future for Nigerian democracy. The post Politicians deceive voters to win elections – Kukah appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Algérie : les importateurs sommés de fournir les données GPS exactes des entrepôts
items.description: Une nouvelle formalité s'ajoute à la longue liste des exigences que doivent satisfaire les importateurs algériens. La nouvelle exigence concerne à la fois les opérateurs qui importent des matières premières pour leurs besoins propres et les importateurs de marchandises destinées à la revente en l’état. Elle concerne la géolocalisation de leurs entrepôts. Les importateurs appelés à rectifier la localisation GPS de leurs entrepôts La mesure est contenue dans une note de la Direction du commerce de la wilaya de Bordj Bou Arreridj à l'adresse des opérateurs économiques concernés par les opérations d'importation. Ces derniers sont sommés de régulariser leur situation concernant la rectification de la localisation GPS de leurs entrepôts de marchandises avant le 25 novembre. La formalité concerne les importateurs ayant obtenu le certificat de respect des exigences. Un ultimatum en lien avec l’affaire des fausses déclarations ? Dans sa note, la direction informe “les opérateurs économiques activant dans le domaine de l’importation de matières premières ou de produits et de marchandises destinés à la revente en l’état, et titulaires d’un certificat de respect des exigences, qu’ils sont tenus de régulariser leur situation en ce qui concerne la correction de la localisation géographique (GPS) des entrepôts déclarés.” La rectification doit se faire avant le 25 du mois en cours via la plateforme numérique consacrée à l’attestation de respect des exigences, dans l'espace réservé à l'opérateur, est-il précisé. L’exigence de la rectification survient quelques semaines après l’annonce de la découverte de dossiers du PPI (programme provisoire d’importation) contenant de fausses informations, avec parfois une même adresse pour plusieurs dizaines de commerçants. L’article Algérie : les importateurs sommés de fournir les données GPS exactes des entrepôts est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: Ghana’s cocaine seizures abroad raise questions about port security, trade integrity and national reputation
items.description: Something is happening, and we cannot afford to treat it as another passing headline! According to JoyNews Research, approximately 13,876 kilogrammes of cocaine linked to Ghana have been seized abroad in five separate operations since January 2025. That is the equivalent weight of 217 bags of cocoa! Now, pause and consider the implications. How do such quantities become associated with our international trade corridors? Are our cargo inspection systems sufficiently robust? What vulnerabilities exist within our ports, shipping documentation, customs procedures and intelligence architecture? And perhaps the most troubling question: If these quantities were intercepted abroad, what does that tell us about the potential scale of trafficking that remains undetected? The figures alone cannot answer that question, but they certainly justify asking it. You see, international cocaine trafficking is not simply a narcotics problem. It is an economic governance, financial integrity and national security problem. Organised criminal networks thrive where institutional weaknesses intersect with lucrative illicit markets. The proceeds can penetrate legitimate businesses through trade-based money laundering, property acquisitions, shell companies and complex financial transactions. Over time, such illicit financial flows can distort competition, compromise regulatory institutions and weaken confidence in the financial system. Imagine the implications for Ghanaian exporters if international trading partners begin subjecting our shipments to heightened scrutiny. Longer clearance periods, increased compliance costs, disrupted supply chains and reputational damage could eventually affect businesses that have absolutely nothing to do with narcotics trafficking. Must legitimate Ghanaian enterprises pay the economic price for the activities of criminal syndicates? And this is where the responsibility of the current administration becomes particularly important. What exactly are we doing differently to strengthen our national anti-narcotics architecture? Are we sufficiently integrating customs intelligence, port surveillance, financial intelligence, beneficial ownership investigations and international law-enforcement cooperation? Are we conducting credible risk-based inspections of high-risk consignments? Are suspicious financial transactions being systematically connected to underlying trade activities? More importantly, when foreign authorities intercept Ghana-linked shipments, do our institutions pursue the entire criminal value chain, including financiers, facilitators, freight intermediaries and ultimate beneficiaries? We must also distinguish between cocaine originating in Ghana, transiting through Ghana and being concealed in shipments without the knowledge of legitimate exporters. These distinctions are essential to credible investigations and accountability. Let us not underestimate the long-term consequences. Countries do not lose their international credibility overnight. Reputational deterioration occurs gradually, particularly when repeated incidents begin to raise questions about institutional effectiveness. Ghana has spent decades positioning itself as a stable investment destination, a regional commercial gateway and a credible participant in international trade. What happens to that positioning if our export corridors become increasingly associated with narcotics trafficking? What happens to investor confidence, correspondent banking relationships, trade financing and our broader ambitions under the AfCFTA? The administration must therefore demonstrate measurable progress through coordinated investigations, stronger preventive controls, successful prosecutions where evidence warrants them and transparent institutional accountability. This is too consequential to reduce to partisan exchanges. My greatest concern is not merely the cocaine being intercepted abroad. It is what repeated Ghana-linked seizures may reveal about vulnerabilities within our economic and security systems. We cannot build a competitive export economy while leaving organised criminal networks opportunities to exploit legitimate trade infrastructure. Neither can we pursue economic transformation without protecting the institutional integrity upon which sustainable development depends. The government must act decisively, and every responsible Ghanaian must demand credible answers. Because the day Ghana becomes more internationally recognisable for cocaine trafficking than for cocoa, gold, innovation and legitimate enterprise, we will have lost something far more valuable than revenue. We will have compromised the credibility of our nation. Dr. Evans Duah Lecturer, University of Skills Training and Entrepreneurial Development

items.title: Burkina/Culture : Jazz à Ouaga revient sous le thème « Jazz et racines africaines »
items.description: Du 27 au 29 novembre 2026, Ouagadougou vibrera au rythme de la 33ᵉ édition du Festival international Jazz à Ouaga. Le programme de ce rendez-vous culturel a été dévoilé au cours d'une conférence de presse du comité d'organisation, ce jeudi 12 novembre 2026 à Ouagadougou. La rencontre a également été l'occasion de présenter le bureau chargé de conduire cette édition. Porté par l'association Jazz à Ouaga, le festival signe son retour en 2026 avec pour thème « Jazz et racines africaines », après une pause en 2024. Cette nouvelle édition se veut ainsi une relance de l'événement, avec l'ambition de réaffirmer la place de l'Afrique comme berceau et terre d'avenir du jazz. Elle entend également célébrer la diversité des expressions jazzistiques sur le continent, favoriser les rencontres et les échanges entre artistes de l'espace AES et, d'ailleurs, tout en contribuant au rayonnement culturel du Burkina Faso. Prévue sur trois jours, cette 33ᵉ édition ambitionne de marquer les esprits et de renouer avec le public autour des sonorités du jazz et de ses racines africaines. Une décision qui s'accompagne d'une programmation artistique mêlant talents nationaux et internationaux. « Nous avons choisi de faire trois jours car c'est une relance. Nous avons commencé les préparatifs et retenu ce format de trois jours de Jazz à Ouaga, avec des artistes nationaux et internationaux », explique Arouna Savadogo, président de l'association Jazz à Ouaga. Selon Arouna Savadogo, le choix des artistes issus des pays membres de l'AES constitue une des particularités de cette 33ᵉ édition La programmation de cette édition de relance s'annonce particulièrement riche en sonorités et en talents. Pour ce grand retour, Jazz à Ouaga entend réunir des artistes de renom, issus des pays membres de l'AES, dont les univers musicaux témoignent de la diversité et de l'évolution du jazz nourri par les traditions africaines. Parmi les têtes d'affiche figure Mamar Kassey, groupe emblématique du Niger. Porté par le chanteur et flûtiste Yacouba Moumouni, le groupe explore l'ethno-jazz en associant les rythmes traditionnels haoussa, djerma, peul et songhaï à des sonorités contemporaines. À travers des instruments traditionnels comme le molo, auxquels s'ajoutent des instruments modernes, notamment la basse électrique, Mamar Kassey propose une fusion musicale inspirée des traditions sahéliennes. Le Mali sera également à l'honneur avec Vieux Farka Touré. Fils du célèbre musicien Ali Farka Touré, il s'inscrit dans la continuité du blues malien tout en lui apportant une touche de modernité. Le guitariste est reconnu pour son jeu virtuose, qui associe les sonorités du blues du désert aux influences du rock et aux rythmes traditionnels sahéliens. Le Burkina Faso sera représenté par plusieurs artistes, dont le duo Sissao et ATT et Audrey Korsaga. « Cette affiche, réunissant des artistes majeurs du Burkina Faso, du Mali et du Niger, réaffirme de manière éclatante la place de notre région dans le dialogue culturel mondial. Elle s'inscrit en parfaite cohérence avec les dynamiques de souveraineté, de solidarité sahélienne et de rayonnement portées par les plus hautes autorités de l'espace de l'Alliance des États du Sahel (AES). La culture devient ainsi un vecteur d'unité et de fierté partagée », confie Lombar Barry, chargé de programmation artistique du festival Jazz à Ouaga. Par ailleurs, la 33ᵉ édition de Jazz à Ouaga prévoit également une conférence publique autour du thème : « Jazz et racines africaines : comment valoriser nos patrimoines musicaux locaux ? ». À entendre les organisateurs, cette rencontre entend ouvrir la réflexion sur les défis liés à la préservation et à la promotion des héritages musicaux africains. La numérisation, la transmission aux jeunes générations, la professionnalisation des acteurs culturels et l'exportation des rythmes traditionnels figurent parmi les principales questions qui seront abordées. Quelques membres du nouveau bureau chargés de conduire la 33ᵉ édition de Jazz à Ouaga À travers cette initiative, ils souhaitent également établir un lien entre la réflexion et les propositions artistiques de cette édition. L'exemple du groupe nigérien Mamar Kassey, qui associe des instruments traditionnels comme le molo aux sonorités contemporaines du jazz-fusion, illustre cette volonté de faire dialoguer patrimoine et modernité. « Valoriser le patrimoine local est au cœur de nos missions. Cela passe notamment par la formation de la relève artistique à travers le concours Jazz performance, mais aussi par la décentralisation de la musique afin de la rendre accessible au plus grand nombre », poursuit Lombar Barry. Placé sous le parrainage du ministre en charge de la communication Pingwendé Gilbert Ouédraogo, le festival international du Jazz à Ouaga va se dérouler sur l'esplanade de la baguette du Faso sise à Ouaga 2000. Pour mémoire, l'association Jazz à Ouaga a pour vocation de promouvoir et de développer la culture jazzistique au Burkina Faso et à l'international. Son bureau exécutif a été renouvelé le 17 juillet 2025, et cette étape a été suivie d'une profonde réforme interne, destinée à instaurer une gouvernance exemplaire, en phase avec une nouvelle vision. Portée par une dynamique associative renouvelée et conforme aux textes en vigueur, l'association rassemble, fédère ses membres et sympathisants autour d'un seul et même objectif. Celui de la promotion de la culture. Leurs objectifs et missions phares sont entre autres : accroître la culture du jazz, cette musique née de l'exil noir et aujourd'hui universelle ; organiser annuellement le festival international Jazz à Ouaga, vitrine de cette ambition ; contribuer au développement de la discipline jazz et à l'enrichissement de la vie culturelle burkinabè, tout en participant au rayonnement international de la ville de Ouagadougou ; former et détecter de nouveaux talents à travers des concours comme « Jazz Performance » ; favoriser les échanges professionnels entre artistes burkinabè et leurs homologues internationaux. L'association célèbre le jazz comme symbole de paix et de dialogue entre toutes les cultures du monde. Muriel Dominique Ouédraogo Lefaso.net

items.title: FG concessions Port Harcourt airport for 30 years, eyes two others
items.description: By Folarin Kehinde The Federal Government has signed a 30-year concession agreement for the Port Harcourt International Airport as part of efforts to attract private investment, improve operational efficiency and unlock the economic potential of the nation’s loss-making airports. The Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo, disclosed this on Thursday in Abuja during the signing of the concession agreement with Port Harcourt Airport Company Limited. Keyamo said the concession was aimed at improving the operational efficiency of the airport, boosting revenue generation and unlocking its commercial potential. He explained that the Federal Government had been using profits generated from major airports to subsidise the operations of other airports that were running at a loss. According to him, the cost of maintaining airports, including personnel expenses, diesel and other operational requirements, has continued to put pressure on government finances. The minister said government lacked the resources to fully develop the non-aeronautical components of some airports, making private sector participation necessary. “Some of our airports are being run at a loss. We make so much money from some of our primary airports, and most of those profits are ploughed into running other airports,” Keyamo said. He noted that the concession had the approval of President Bola Tinubu and the Federal Executive Council, adding that the process was not a sudden decision but one that successive administrations had struggled to implement. Keyamo said previous attempts to concession airports were frustrated by resistance from labour unions and court cases involving the government. He, however, attributed the successful conclusion of the process to negotiations with aviation unions, saying the government had secured their agreement before signing the deal. The minister assured workers that the concession would not lead to job losses or a reduction in their conditions of service. He said Tinubu had directed that the welfare of aviation workers must be protected throughout the concession process. “President Bola Tinubu was very concerned about that, that no worker should lose his job. The conditions of service should remain the same,” he said. Keyamo added that the concessionaire would be subjected to performance reviews every five years to ensure compliance with the terms of the agreement. He warned that the government could take back the airport if the concessionaire failed to meet the agreed standards. The minister also disclosed that the government had received proposals from investors interested in developing other airports, including those in Benin and Yola. He said the government was considering the proposals as part of efforts to make more airports commercially viable. Keyamo identified bureaucratic bottlenecks in public institutions as another reason for involving private investors in airport management. He argued that private operators could make decisions faster, attract capital and introduce innovative commercial activities capable of increasing revenue. According to him, airports have significant revenue opportunities beyond passenger and aircraft-related charges, particularly through shopping malls, supermarkets, conference centres and other commercial facilities. He cited the potential of the Port Harcourt airport, noting that its location around the Gulf of Guinea could make it a major regional aviation hub. Speaking on behalf of the concessionaire, Group Executive of R28 Holdings, Eyo Asuquo, said the company would bring international standards and improved facilities to the airport. Asuquo described the concession process as rigorous, saying the investors had undertaken extensive engagements within and outside Nigeria to demonstrate their capacity to execute the project. He assured Nigerians that the agreement would not result in staff retrenchment, adding that the expansion of the airport would create additional employment opportunities. He said the company’s ambition was to transform the facility into an airport city and position Port Harcourt as a major hub for the Gulf of Guinea. Asuquo added that the company would open up investment opportunities to other interested stakeholders to support the development of the airport. items.title: Tinubu: Wike inaugurates Rivers campaign council, directs it to recruit 5 new voters daily
items.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: The Minister of the Federal Capital Territory FCT, Nyesom Wike, has inaugurated the Presidential Campaign Council for Rivers State and directed its members to recruit at least five new voters daily to deliver votes for President Bola Tinubu in the 2027 election. Wike, who performed the inauguration on Thursday, set a target of three million votes for the president in the state. He called for hard work, focus and issue-based campaigning, and dismissed recent confusion over appointments into the committees. “I am sure by Monday the list of the chairmen and members of the various sub-committees will have been prepared so that the chairmen can kick-start by inviting their various committee members. It is very important,” he said. The minister said victory in Rivers was not in doubt. “Everybody knows that we are going to win election in Rivers State. So we are not talking about winning now,” he said. Wike recalled how the three million figure came up in a discussion with Senate President Godswill Akpabio. “He said, ‘How much is the registered votes here?’ I said, ‘over three million.’ He said, ‘Okay, you will bring three million.’ I said, ‘Well, we will try’. I know that three million, if we work hard, it ia easy.” Wike urged members of the council to treat their appointments as an opportunity to work for the Rainbow Coalition, and called on them to stay united and disciplined in the face of provocation from the opposition. He cited the Olubadan and former governor of Oyo State, Oba Rasheed Ladoja who he said spoke a day earlier when the National Working Committee of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) paid him a courtesy visit in Oyo State. “He said if he was still in politics, if he was not a traditional ruler today, he would have joined Rainbow Coalition, that is the best way to bring every shade of opinion, members of other political parties to join hands to make sure that Mr. President is re-elected come 2027,” Wike said. Governor Siminalayi Fubara of Rivers State described the new council as bigger, wider and better coordinated than the structure that delivered victory for the president in 2023. He said former political adversaries had now closed ranks to work together for the state and the president. “Nothing is impossible. The only thing that is not possible is to revive the dead. If we take this as a serious task that must be achieved, we will come out decisively with a stronger vote than what we did in 2023,” Fubara said. The governor assured members who were left out that they would be accommodated in the subcommittees. He also warned against double-dealing and urged members to work with sincerity rather than profess loyalty in public while sabotaging the effort behind closed doors. “I am here, and I say it boldly anywhere, any day, in private and in secret: I have taken this position,” Fubara said. items.title: Imo East: Court orders INEC to recognise Nwole as NDC candidate
items.description: By Ikechukwu Nnochiri ABUJA – The Federal High Court in Abuja has ordered the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to immediately recognise and publish the name of Uche Nwole as the candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) for the Imo East senatorial election scheduled for January 16, 2027. In a judgment delivered by Justice Mohammed Umar, the court said it was satisfied that the plaintiff, Nwole, was the bona fide winner of a primary election conducted by the party, which it noted was duly monitored by INEC. It held that, in view of Sections 84(1) and (2) and 86 of the Electoral Act 2026, the NDC ought to have nominated and forwarded the plaintiff’s name to the electoral body as its senatorial candidate. According to the court, the NDC could not lawfully nominate a consensus candidate other than the one who emerged from its INEC-monitored primary election. Consequently, aside from issuing an order of perpetual injunction restraining the party from nominating or submitting any other name for the election, the court barred INEC from accepting, listing or publishing any purported NDC candidate who allegedly emerged from a primary election that was never held or monitored by the commission, or any purported consensus candidate whose nomination breached Sections 87(1) and (3) of the Electoral Act 2026. The judgment followed suit number FHC/ABJ/CS/1225/2026, in which the NDC, INEC and Hon. Onyeagucha Uchechukwu were the 1st to 3rd defendants. The plaintiff alleged that although he secured the highest number of valid votes cast in the primary election, the party sidelined him and chose the 3rd defendant as its flag bearer for the senatorial poll. Justice Umar said that, after careful examination of all the evidence adduced in the matter, he was satisfied that the plaintiff’s case deserved to succeed. He therefore granted all seven principal reliefs the plaintiff sought. Among other things, the court held: “A declaration is made that, upon the construction of the clear, unambiguous and express provisions, spirit and tenor of Sections 84(1) and (2) and 86 of the Electoral Act 2026, the 1st Defendant duly conducted primary elections, which were duly monitored by the 2nd Defendant, for all aspirants seeking to be nominated as the candidate of the party to contest the elective position of Senator representing Imo East Senatorial District in the 2027 general election. “A declaration is made that, upon a careful construction and interpretation of Section 87(1), (2) and (3) of the Electoral Act 2026, the 1st Defendant, having conducted a primary election in accordance with Sections 84(1) and (2) and 86 of the Electoral Act, cannot lawfully nominate a consensus candidate to contest the office of Senator representing Imo East Senatorial District in the 2027 general election. “A declaration is made that the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), being a body established by law, must at all times obey its constitution; respect, observe and implement its own guidelines, rules and regulations; and comply with the provisions of the Electoral Act and the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria 1999 (as amended) in all its programmes and activities. “An order is granted mandating the 1st Defendant to immediately forward the Plaintiff’s name to the 2nd Defendant as its duly elected candidate, who emerged from the primary election monitored by the 2nd Defendant and conducted in accordance with Sections 84(1) and (2) and 86 of the Electoral Act 2026, to contest the office of Senator representing Imo East Senatorial District in the 2027 general election. “An order of perpetual injunction is granted restraining the 1st Defendant from nominating or submitting any name other than the Plaintiff’s, and restraining, barring and prohibiting the 2nd Defendant from accepting, listing and publishing in the final list of candidates any purported candidate from the 1st Defendant who magically emerged from a purported primary election that was never held and never monitored by the 2nd Defendant, or any purported consensus candidate presented by the 1st Defendant whose nomination breached the law and does not comply with the express provisions of Sections 87(1) and (3) of the Electoral Act 2026, to contest the office of Senator representing Imo East Senatorial District in the 2027 general election.” The post Imo East: Court orders INEC to recognise Nwole as NDC candidate appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: 2027: Tinubu has no competitor in South-South — Akpabio
items.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Senate President Godswill Akpabio has said President Bola Tinubu faces no serious competition in the South-South ahead of the 2027 presidential election, citing regional support for the All Progressives Congress (APC) and projects he said the President had delivered. Akpabio made the remarks while campaigning for Tinubu’s re-election at the APC presidential campaign rally at Samuel Ogbemudia Stadium in Benin City, Edo State on Thursday, pointing to the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway, security initiatives and infrastructure projects in Edo as reasons residents should support Tinubu. “I want you to know that President Bola Tinubu has no competition, no competitor equally in the whole of the South-South. We are grateful for the Lagos-Calabar coastal highway, we had that as a dream but it never came to fruition until he came to office. He has even added another 100 kilometers to cover the entirety of Edo and Edo people are very grateful,” Akpabio said. He also urged South-South voters to turn out for Tinubu on January 16, 2027, saying the region intended to outpoll other parts of the country. “Your Excellency, the Vice President, I want you to know that this is my zone. And we have resolved in this zone that no other zone in Nigeria will beat this zone. We will vote massively for the President come 16th of January 2027. “We will beat other zones if care is not taken. We may even beat your zone, the North East zone of the country. We will vote even against all odds,” he said. Akpabio said Edo was firmly behind Tinubu, recalling that Vice-President Kashim Shettima had told him the state’s election was “over.” He also described Edo as the first ACN/APC state in the South-South and said all states in the region were now governed by the party. “I must also say that the Vice president whispered to me when we came in here that Edo is over, election in Edo is over. When the Governor of Edo, Gov. Okpebholo started shouting, a lot of people did not understand him. Why will Edo not return President Bola Ahmed Tinubu into office? Not just the love he has for this state. “This state happens to have been the pioneer ACN/APC state in the South-South part of Nigeria. From Edo today, all the states of the South-South are now APC,” Akpabio added. He also cited security measures, including a new mobile police base, the recruitment of forest guards and plans for state police, as evidence of efforts to improve safety in Edo and across Nigeria. “He has, in terms of security, he has turned the army forward oppression base. They now have a new Mopo base, Mopo 82 squadron, to cater for the security of Edo people. “They have recruited over 500 forest guards from amongst our youth. And the Governor has told me that as soon as we commence the state police, which about 32 states have met their returns and approved already, to alter the constitution of Nigeria, to bring in for the first time in the history of this country, state policing, as part and parcel to complement what the federal police is doing. So security is coming back to Nigeria in full force. “For Edo, he has established another division here, 83 Army Division, to cater for the good people of Edo. The President, we thank you on behalf of South-South because these things are happening. Many universities have also been established here,” he said. Akpabio praised the South-South governors’ support for Tinubu and pointed to ongoing construction projects in the region, including new flyovers in Edo. “The greatest of all is the appreciation and the commitment of our state governors in the South-South. Almost every place has been turned into a construction site. In Edo, the first set of flyovers are already springing up,” he added. items.title: Nigeria’s exports to China rise 81% to $2.25bn
items.description: By Favour Ulebor, Abuja Nigeria’s exports to China rose by 81 per cent to $2.25 billion in the first half of 2026, while bilateral trade between both countries increased by 35 per cent to $17.4 billion, the Chinese Embassy has said. The Cultural Counsellor of the Chinese Embassy in Nigeria and Director of the China Cultural Centre in Nigeria, Mr Yang Jiaxing, disclosed this on Thursday in Abuja at the 2026 launch ceremony of the Voice of Nigeria (VON) China-Nigeria Bridge Programme. Yang attributed the growth to expanding economic cooperation between the two countries, saying China’s zero-tariff policy for 53 African countries, including Nigeria, which took effect in May 2026, would create more opportunities for Nigerian exports. He said China’s trade with African countries reached $207.4 billion in the first half of 2026, while imports from the continent rose to $28.5 billion between May and June. According to him, imports from Nigeria recorded year-on-year growth of more than 40 per cent in both May and June, reflecting stronger trade relations between the two countries. He said: “In the first half of this year, bilateral trade between China and Nigeria reached $17.4 billion, up 35 per cent year-on-year. China’s imports from Nigeria amounted to $2.25 billion, representing a remarkable increase of 81 per cent.” Yang described the China-Nigeria Bridge Programme as a platform for promoting cultural understanding, media cooperation and closer relations between citizens of both countries. The programme, jointly initiated by the Chinese Embassy, the Africa Regional Bureau of Xinhua News Agency and VON, provides Mandarin lessons and reports on China-Africa relations. Also speaking, the Director-General of VON, Jibrin Baba Ndace, said the introduction of Mandarin as the organisation’s ninth broadcast language would strengthen Nigeria’s international presence and enable it to communicate its stories to a wider audience. Ndace, who was represented by the Director of General Services, Alhaji Danladi Abubakar, said the service would promote Nigeria’s culture, tourism, business opportunities and national image among Chinese-speaking audiences. He said the initiative followed agreements reached between Nigeria and China at the 2024 Forum on China-Africa Cooperation held in Beijing. According to him, VON also signed agreements with Xinhua News Agency and the Chinese Embassy in 2026 to promote content sharing, staff training, broadcasting capacity and media cooperation. In his remarks, the Executive Secretary of the Nigeria Press Council, Dili Ezughah, described the programme as an important step towards strengthening cultural diplomacy and people-to-people relations. He urged the partners to sustain the initiative, saying its success should be measured by its ability to promote mutual understanding and lasting relationships between citizens of both countries. items.title: Ododo flags off 38.5km Kogi road project
items.description: …Promises to End Decades of Poor Access By Soni Daniel, Northern Region Editor Kogi State Governor, Alhaji Ahmed Usman Ododo, on Thursday flagged off the construction of the 38.5-kilometre Kabba–Olle-Bunu–Iluke-Bunu Road in Kabba/Bunu Local Government Area, promising to address decades of poor road infrastructure in the area. The project, flagged off at Oke-Ofin, is expected to improve connectivity among communities in Bunu land, ease the movement of agricultural produce and expand access to economic opportunities. Speaking at the ceremony, Ododo described the project as the fulfilment of a long-standing aspiration of the people, assuring residents that his administration would not abandon any community, irrespective of its location. He said the road would mark a new chapter for the area by reconnecting communities that had remained isolated for years. The governor recalled how the deplorable condition of the road had affected farmers, businesses and residents, explaining that farmers struggled to transport their produce to markets, while indigenes living outside the state found it difficult to visit their ancestral homes. He disclosed that his personal experience during a visit to Iluke-Bunu following a security incident involving students had strengthened his resolve to rehabilitate the road. Ododo said the project was part of his administration’s commitment to complementing efforts to restore security with tangible development, stressing that peace without infrastructure and economic opportunities would remain incomplete. According to him, the road would facilitate the transportation of yams, cassava, cashew and other agricultural produce, reduce transportation costs, shorten travel time and stimulate commercial activities across Bunu land. The governor acknowledged the support of President Bola Tinubu, saying the increased financial resources available to state governments following the Federal Government’s economic reforms had helped subnational governments execute major infrastructure projects. He urged residents to embrace unity and take ownership of the project by monitoring its execution, protecting construction equipment and ensuring that quality standards were maintained. The Commissioner for Information and Communications, Kingsley Femi Fanwo, described the flag-off as a historic moment, citing his personal connection to Bunu land. Fanwo recalled trekking from Iluke to Ole-Bunu because of the poor condition of the road, which he said had remained in a deplorable state for more than 35 years. He said the project would open up several communities in Bunu to greater economic and social opportunities, adding that future generations would remember the intervention. The Commissioner for Education, an indigene of the benefiting community, also thanked the governor, describing the project as a major development for residents who had endured years of hardship because of the inaccessible road. He said the road’s completion would improve the transportation of agricultural produce, attract businesses, support existing investments in electricity and education, and help reduce criminal activities by improving movement and accessibility. The commissioner assured the governor that communities along the route would cooperate to protect the contractor’s personnel and equipment. Speaking on behalf of the contractor, the Kogi State Project Supervisor of TEC Engineering, Simon Xu, said the project had an 18-month completion period. Xu assured the government and residents that the company was committed to delivering quality work, noting that its experience in Nigeria and the availability of equipment and personnel would support timely execution. He also appealed to host communities to cooperate with the company and ensure the safety of workers and construction equipment throughout the project period. items.title: 194 make first class as UNIZIK graduates 16,842
items.description: By Vincent Ujumadu AWKA — Nnamdi Azikiwe University (UNIZIK), Awka, Anambra State, will graduate 16,842 students at its 20th and 21st combined convocation ceremonies scheduled for November 15 to 20, 2026, with 194 of the graduands earning First Class honours. The Vice-Chancellor, Prof. Ugochukwu Bond Anyaehie, disclosed this during a pre-convocation press briefing in Awka, where he also highlighted the institution’s academic, administrative, technological and infrastructural achievements. Anyaehie said the graduands comprised 14,803 first-degree recipients and 2,039 postgraduate students from the 2025 and 2026 academic sessions. A breakdown of the results showed that 4,230 students obtained Second Class Upper Division, while 7,992 graduated with Second Class Lower Division. Another 1,936 students obtained Third Class honours, while 65 graduated with Pass degrees. A further 486 earned unclassified medical and professional degrees. At the postgraduate level, 603 candidates obtained Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) degrees, 29 earned Master of Philosophy/PhD degrees, 1,113 obtained Master’s degrees, while 294 graduated with Postgraduate Diplomas (PGDs). The Vice-Chancellor described the forthcoming convocation as an opportunity to celebrate the university’s growth and showcase achievements recorded under his administration’s vision of making a greater UNIZIK possible. He said the university had been ranked joint fourth among Nigerian universities in the Times Higher Education (THE) World University Rankings. He also disclosed that UNIZIK’s debate team won the 13th All Nigerian Universities Debate Championship (ANUDC), marking the first time the institution had clinched the title. Anyaehie recalled that the university’s athletes also won silver and bronze medals at the 12th Federation of African University Sports (FASU) Games held in Cairo, Egypt. On digital infrastructure, he said the university had been selected for the Federal Government’s $617.7 million Investment in Digital and Creative Enterprises (iDICE) programme, supported by the Bank of Industry, Agence Française de Développement and the African Development Bank/Islamic Development Bank. He said the institution had expanded its internet bandwidth to 2Gbps through the Agence Française de Développement-Nigeria Research and Education Network (AFD-NgREN), adding that equipment supplied by Galaxy Backbone had been installed to activate an additional 300Mbps. The Vice-Chancellor further disclosed that his administration had established a TETFund ICT Experience Centre at Hall 2 of the university’s Digital Library to support training and research in artificial intelligence, robotics, cybersecurity and software engineering. He said the university had also upgraded its computer laboratories with 200 all-in-one desktop computers, 20 high-performance laptops, interactive smart screens, servers, enterprise network switches and video conferencing equipment. On administrative reforms, Anyaehie said the institution had introduced an online graduate clearance system to eliminate delays associated with physical clearance procedures and accelerate the issuance of statements of results. He added that the university had digitised its historical registries, academic results and transcript archives to make students’ academic records easier to retrieve. According to him, the administration had also revamped the Vice-Chancellor’s student portal to provide direct and real-time communication between students and the university management. On medical education, Anyaehie said the university had secured full re-accreditation from the Medical and Dental Council of Nigeria (MDCN), leading to an increase in its annual admission quota for Bachelor of Medicine and Bachelor of Surgery (MBBS) students from 100 to 300. He added that the university was upgrading its Medical Centre to operate as a 24-hour emergency facility and provide residency programmes. Other interventions, he said, included expanding closed-circuit television (CCTV) coverage and perimeter lighting to strengthen campus security, rehabilitating hostel water systems and restrooms, and providing weekly diesel allocations for hostel generators. The Vice-Chancellor urged the graduating students to uphold the values of discipline, self-reliance and excellence as they prepared to face challenges beyond the university. He said their academic achievements reflected the institution’s commitment to producing graduates worthy in character and learning. UNIZIK became a federal university in 1992. It was named after Nigeria’s first President, Dr Nnamdi Azikiwe, and evolved from the former Anambra State University of Technology (ASUTECH). The post 194 make first class as UNIZIK graduates 16,842 appeared first on Vanguard News .
