items.title: Immigration sets 5 targets for new Comptrollers, as IGP seeks stronger partnership
items.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: The Comptroller General of the Nigeria Immigration Service NIS, Kemi Nandap, has set five “non-negotiable” expectations for newly promoted Comptrollers, ordering them to lead by example, deliver measurable results, protect the Service’s integrity, embrace reforms and develop their personnel. The Inspector General of Police IGP, Olatunji Disu, also pledged the Nigeria Police Force’s commitment to a stronger partnership with the Service. Both spoke on Thursday at the decoration of 94 new Comptrollers of Immigration. A total of 106 officers were promoted, but 12 retired before the ceremony. Nandap told the officers that their new rank came with heavier demands. “Promotion is not simply a reward for what you have accomplished. It is a declaration of confidence in what you are now expected to do,” she said. She said the rank was “a greater burden of trust” and a higher standard of conduct. “I have some expectations of you, and they are non-negotiable. First, you must lead by example. Two, you must deliver measurable results. Thirdly, protect the integrity of the service. Fourth, embrace innovation and institutional reforms. Change starts with you. Your attitude matters. And lastly, number five, develop your people. You must build competent and motivated and disciplined teams that are capable of sustaining progress of the service”, she demanded. The Comptroller General said the expectations were not ceremonial. “They are practical standards against which your leadership should be assessed. And I urge you to personally hold yourself accountable,” she said. She told the officers that the Service needed more than senior officers. It needs more effective leaders, Nandap said. “Corruption, extortion, abuse of office, professional negligence, and indiscipline have no place in the Nigerian immigration service we have built here. I expect every controller to demonstrate zero tolerance for misconduct. You cannot demand integrity from your subordinates while compromising your own principles”, she added. According to her, ongoing reforms were meant to make the Service professional, intelligence-led and technologically enabled. She cited the e-Border Solution, the Border Control and Immigration Management System (BCIMS) and the e-Gates among the digital platforms being deployed. But she cautioned that technology alone would not deliver results. “Our technology, no matter how sophisticated, cannot compensate for weak leadership, poor information, indiscipline, or the lack of accountability,” she said. She told the Comptrollers to ensure the reforms reached commands, border posts and airports. “You must take ownership of the systems entrusted to your formations. You must ensure that officers are properly trained,” she said. The Comptroller General also urged the officers to treat the public with respect. “Behind every passport application, every border crossing, every immigration inquiry, and every interaction with the public is a person who deserves to be treated with dignity, fairness, and respect. Do not wait for the headquarters to identify every problem before you now have to deal with the real issues. But above all, you have to be worthy of the confidence that this promotion represents,” she added. Disu, in his remarks, said the work of both agencies was tied to national security. “When the Nigerian Immigration Service shares information with other security agencies, it enhances our national security and protects our citizens,” he said. He said the mandates of the two agencies were “interconnected,” and pointed to collaboration and intelligence sharing as areas of cooperation. “I wish to reaffirm the commitment of the Nigeria Police Force to strengthen this continued partnership for greater security of our country,” the IGP said. items.title: Kudus, Ayew and Partey return: What changes for the Black Stars?
items.description: After back-to-back defeats, the Black Stars are determined to restore the pride and legacy that once defined them. The four-time champions suffered a difficult start in the qualifiers, with a 2-0 defeat to Côte d’Ivoire in Bouaké before losing 4-2 to Gambia on home soil. Ghana now sits at the bottom of Group C with zero points and very little hope of returning to the continental showpiece. The Black Stars will host Somalia today, November 12, at the Essipong Sports Stadium, followed by a return fixture on November 16. The national team was weakened after key players suffered injuries and others due to other issues. Kim Lars Bjorkegen, who serves as interim head coach of the Black Stars, named his squad on Tuesday, November 10. Among the names were some of the people the nation missed during the previous games, such as Mohammed Kudus, Jordan Ayew, Mohammed Salisu and Thomas Partey. This game is a must-win, and the Black Stars are desperate to rekindle the love for football and the hopes Ghanaians have in the national team ahead of the crucial double-header against Somalia. Ghana’s captain, Jordan Ayew, returns to the national team, reclaiming the captain’s armband after missing two matches, both of which ended in defeat. As Ghana’s third-highest goal scorer in history, Ayew’s presence is especially vital at this moment. His leadership will be key in motivating the squad to believe in themselves and persevere through challenges. Beyond his leadership qualities, Ayew brings invaluable experience, tenacity, and grit, contributing significantly from kick-off to the final whistle and inspiring his teammates throughout the match. Mohammed Kudus plays for the first time in 2026, bringing a blend of creativity, goal-scoring prowess, and the ability to beat defenders with ease. His speed and vision allow him to move the ball swiftly through midfield, forcing opponents into costly mistakes. Beyond his technical skills and talent, Kudus’ presence provides a significant confidence boost to the new players, serving as an inspiring figure with his global experience. Thomas Partey’s defensive strength, composure, and ability to launch quick attacks by distributing the ball to the wingers bring discipline and calm to the pitch. With the stakes high, Ghana’s midfield trio may give fans hope that they can overcome Somalia, as these qualities help create the balance needed to put G\hana back on a winning path. Buoyed by strong home support and the return of key players, the Black Stars face mounting pressure to deliver a decisive victory. Failure is not an option, and expectations are high. Will the glory return to Essipong, or will Ghana be left searching for answers once more?

items.title: Ntim Fordjour alleges $3bn worth of narcotics linked to Ghana seized abroad since Mahama took office
items.description: Rev. John Ntim Fordjour has alleged that more than US$3 billion worth of drugs linked to Ghana have been seized abroad during President John Dramani Mahama’s tenure, warning that the country’s reputation is being damaged by repeated international narcotics interceptions. The Ranking Member on Parliament’s Defence and Interior Committee made the claim in a post on X on Thursday, November 12, following the latest seizure of 2,600 kilogrammes of cocaine in Spain from a consignment of coconuts shipped from Ghana. He argued that major drug busts involving consignments linked to Ghana had been reported overseas almost every month since President Mahama’s April 1, 2025, post on the government’s zero-tolerance stance on drug trafficking. The Assin South MP further accused government officials, drug networks and state agencies of benefiting from the trade, while demanding that the President act decisively to halt the activities and protect Ghana’s international standing. The latest Spanish seizure involved cocaine hidden in false compartments beneath wooden boxes carrying coconuts. The shipment was loaded at Tema on August 2 and arrived in Valencia on August 22. Two people have been arrested in Spain, but authorities have not announced any arrests in Ghana or identified Ghanaian nationals as suspects.

items.title: Naqvi suggests referendum as 'solution' to debate on new administrative units
items.description: Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi on Thursday suggested that political parties hold a referendum to gauge the public’s opinion on the creation of new administrative units or provinces, terming it the “solution” to the ongoing debate. The security czar has whipped up a political storm over the past few months since he called for the formation of new administrative units in the country, saying the current “system” of governance had “collapsed” and needed a “reset”. Replying to a media query at the National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA) in Lahore on Thursday, Naqvi noted that each political party had a right to disagree with another party or individual. At the same time, he observed that all parties stressed democracy and the supremacy of the people. Therefore, he said: “My only request to all political parties is that this is such an issue […] so they should hold a referendum. “Whatever the public’s opinion in the referendum is; if the public says [new units] should not be created, I am 100 per cent with them that they should not be created. [But], if the public says they should be made, then they should.” Naqvi noted that political parties had varying stances on the debate, with the PPP “having its own stance [and] some parties having their own stance while not saying anything officially”. He again stressed that the solution was to take public opinion into account, suggesting that if there was a proposal for a “better solution”, that should also be presented to the people. Acknowledging the importance of allies in the ruling coalition, he said: “Everyone is a part of this government, and nothing will happen against their will. And if something does happen, then it will be after taking everyone’s consensus.” “My only recommendation is that if we were to conclude this debate, then we should just take the people’s opinion,” he said. The minister had also affirmed in September that any new administrative units would only be formed with the public’s consent, while also doubling down on his call for new provinces. Naqvi claims he and Bilawal ‘nearly on same page’ Responding to another question, Naqvi recalled recent remarks by PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari, wherein he had called for a “political reset” and encouraged unity among political parties. The security czar contended that he and Bilawal were “nearly on the same page”. “He (Bilawal) said that political matters are about to be reset, while my suggestion is that overall matters are about to be reset,” Naqvi elaborated. In his remarks on Tuesday, the Bhutto scion had called for a “political reset”, wherein all political parties must unite for the sake of the country, rather than indulge in “unnecessary debates”. His call for political unity followed exchanges of harsh remarks in recent weeks between federal ministers and veteran politician Maulana Fazlur Rehman, who has now decided to strengthen his ties with the opposition. The PPP chairman also questioned the need for “new experiments” when the country was confronted with much bigger challenges, particularly the economic crisis arising from the Middle East tensions. The same day, PPP’s Punjab chapter also strongly rejected any move towards the creation of new provinces, asserting that doing so will neither address soaring inflation nor rampant unemployment. While Naqvi said he and Bilawal largely shared the same views, the PPP chairman in September had called for a parliamentary debate on the creation of new provinces. “So instead of [speaking at] business forums, Mohsin Naqvi should visit [Parliament],” he had remarked, an apparent reference to the first instance of Naqvi stressing the need for more administrative units while speaking at the Pakistan Economic Summit 2026 in July. PPP, which rules Sindh and is also an ally of the PML-N government at the Centre, has strongly opposed the creation of a new province within Sindh. It has also maintained that any decision on the subject must be taken through the constitutional and parliamentary processes with political consensus. Defence Minister Khawaja Asif’s recent statement regarding the creation of 12 more provinces has also added to the debate on administrative units started by Naqvi. ‘Corruption exists across entire Pakistan’ In his talk with reporters, Naqvi was also asked about federal minister Chaudhry Salik’s recent remarks over alleged corruption in Punjab. In response, he said: “If someone is saying that no corruption is taking place in Pakistan, then apologies but corruption exists across the entire country and it is our responsibility to end it.” The interior minister stressed the importance of highlighting corruption where it was present. The conversation on corruption started after PML-Q’s Salik criticised the incumbent Punjab government led by PML-N, alleging that he regularly heard complaints of corruption. Incensed by his remarks, Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz sent a Rs5 billion defamation notice to Salik for levelling allegations of corruption against her government and demanded that he retract his remarks. Naqvi was also asked about a Capital Development Authority (CDA) notice issued in relation to the residence of the JUI-F chief, which he defended, stating, “This (CDA) campaign has been ongoing for months, and it is not against a certain individual.”

items.title: Casablanca dans le noir : Belfkih évoque un « incident rare »
items.description: Plusieurs quartiers de Casablanca ont été privés de courant mercredi en fin de journée, en pleine tempête. Le porte-parole du Gouvernement a expliqué que les vents violents avaient fait tomber trois câbles haute tension, dont le câble principal, coupant l’électricité pendant près de trois heures. Un incident rare, a-t-il souligné. Lors du point de presse hebdomadaire tenu ce jeudi 12 novembre à l’issue du Conseil de gouvernement, Samir Belfkih, ministre de l’Aménagement du territoire national, de l’Urbanisme, de l’Habitat et de la Politique de la ville, porte-parole du Gouvernement, a répondu aux questions des journalistes sur la coupure d’électricité survenue la veille dans la capitale économique. Il en a imputé la cause aux vents violents. L’incident s’est produit, a-t-il expliqué, dans le contexte des perturbations météorologiques qu’a connues la ville. Les rafales ont provoqué la chute de trois câbles haute tension, dont le câble principal, ce qui a entraîné une interruption de l’alimentation d’environ trois heures avant le retour du courant. Le ministre a parlé d’un « incident rare ». Il a également rendu hommage aux équipes mobilisées pour rétablir le service. Compte tenu de la taille de la métropole, la remise en marche en quelque trois heures représente, à ses yeux, « une grande réussite ». Pouvoir d’achat : des mesures déjà en place et d’autres à venir Interrogé sur la cherté de la vie, le porte-parole a placé la lutte contre la hausse des prix et la préservation du pouvoir d’achat des citoyens et des citoyennes en tête des priorités de l’action gouvernementale. Il a rattaché les augmentations enregistrées sur les carburants à l’évolution des cours sur les marchés internationaux. L’Exécutif suit la situation par l’intermédiaire de comités interministériels chargés de surveiller l’évolution des prix. Samir Belfkih a relevé que les indicateurs internationaux ont amorcé une tendance baissière, un mouvement qui devrait, a-t-il indiqué, se répercuter sur le marché national dans les prochains jours. Il a ensuite passé en revue plusieurs dispositions déjà arrêtées pour atténuer les effets du renchérissement. Une enveloppe de 400 millions de dirhams a été débloquée en faveur des professionnels du transport routier, afin de limiter l’impact des coûts de transport sur les prix des produits et des biens de consommation. Le Gouvernement a aussi décidé de suspendre temporairement l’exportation de certains produits dont les prix ont nettement progressé sur le marché intérieur, une décision destinée à renforcer l’offre nationale et à alléger la pression sur les prix. Sur le plan social, le ministre a annoncé que le Conseil de gouvernement a adopté ce jeudi un décret relevant le montant de l’aide sociale directe à compter de janvier prochain, pour le porter à 600 dirhams. Cette revalorisation s’inscrit dans les engagements pris par le Gouvernement au titre du renforcement de la protection sociale. Le porte-parole a prévenu que l’action de l’Exécutif ne s’arrêtera pas aux mesures déjà dévoilées. Elle comprendra des interventions immédiates et continues, ajustées à la tournure que prendront les prix. Il n’est pas envisageable, a-t-il affirmé, de laisser les citoyens seuls face aux conséquences de la vie chère. Samir Belfkih a enfin souligné que le Gouvernement a commencé à tenir sa promesse de rehausser l’aide sociale directe quatre semaines à peine après son installation. La défense du pouvoir d’achat, a-t-il assuré, demeurera au cœur des décisions et des dispositions à venir. items.title: Environnement à Siguiri : Alphonse Charles Wright dénonce l’inaction et réclame des comptes à tous les niveaux
items.description: Le procureur spécial de la Cour de répression des infractions économiques et financières (CRIEF), Alphonse Charles Wright, a vivement interpellé les autorités sur la dégradation de l’environnement dans la préfecture de Siguiri, marquée notamment par les conséquences de l’exploitation minière. Invité exceptionnel de nos confrères de Télé 24, ce jeudi 12 novembre 2026, il a livré son analyse de la situation, dénoncé les insuffisances dans la protection des populations et appelé à une prise de responsabilité à tous les niveaux de l’administration. A Siguiri, une situation environnementale préoccupante Pour Alphonse Charles Wright, la situation environnementale à Siguiri ne date pas d’aujourd’hui. Il affirme avoir personnellement effectué des déplacements sur le terrain afin de constater l’ampleur des dégâts, au-delà des images et des commentaires relayés sur les réseaux sociaux. Le procureur spécial décrit un environnement particulièrement éprouvant pour les populations, caractérisé par une chaleur suffocante, une importante présence de poussière et la pollution des cours d’eau, des fleuves et des marigots. Une situation qui, selon lui, expose les habitants à des risques sanitaires, notamment des maladies pulmonaires, et menace directement leurs conditions de vie. « Quand vous partez à Siguiri, le premier élément du déclin climatique que vous sentez, c’est cette chaleur suffocante, la poussière, avec le développement de toutes sortes de maladies pulmonaires », a-t-il expliqué. Il déplore également l’état de dégradation des ressources hydriques, estimant que la pollution des cours d’eau constitue une menace majeure pour les populations. « Pas d’eau, pas de vie », a-t-il rappelé, soulignant la nécessité de s’attaquer aux causes profondes du problème plutôt que de se limiter à des réactions ponctuelles. « Il faut s’attaquer au problème à la racine » Le procureur spécial a notamment dénoncé les interventions limitées dans le temps et les réactions qui, selon lui, ne permettent pas d’apporter des solutions durables à la crise environnementale de Siguiri. Evoquant une vidéo attribuée à un ressortissant burkinabè, dans laquelle celui-ci aurait affirmé vouloir contribuer à la destruction de l’environnement guinéen pour développer le Burkina Faso, Alphonse Charles Wright a estimé que cette séquence ne devait pas faire oublier l’ancienneté du problème. Pour lui, la dégradation environnementale ne peut être réduite à une vidéo devenue virale sur les réseaux sociaux. La question mérite plutôt une réponse structurelle, fondée sur des responsabilités clairement établies et des mesures concrètes. Les autorités administratives appelées à rendre des comptes Alphonse Charles Wright a également mis en cause les insuffisances dans la gestion administrative et la protection de l’environnement. Il estime que les responsabilités doivent être recherchées à tous les échelons, depuis les autorités locales jusqu’aux services techniques et au département chargé des Mines. Il a notamment évoqué le rôle des préfets, sous-préfets, présidents de district et responsables administratifs dans le contrôle des activités minières et la protection des populations. Le magistrat a, par ailleurs, relevé l’existence de pratiques coutumières non écrites qui encadreraient certaines activités dans les localités concernées. Selon ses explications, ces pratiques doivent être examinées, afin de mieux comprendre les relations entre les exploitants, les communautés et les autorités locales. Il a ainsi insisté sur la nécessité de confronter les différentes versions et de recueillir les éléments permettant d'établir les responsabilités de chacun, plutôt que de prendre des décisions sur la base de témoignages isolés. La protection des populations au cœur des préoccupations Pour le procureur spécial, la protection de l’environnement et de la santé des populations ne doit pas être reléguée au second plan. Il estime que les autorités compétentes ont l’obligation d’intervenir lorsque les conditions de vie des citoyens sont menacées. Il a également souligné que la lutte contre les atteintes à l’environnement nécessite une coordination entre les différentes structures administratives et techniques, ainsi qu’une application effective des règles en vigueur. A travers cette sortie médiatique, Alphonse Charles Wright entend remettre au centre du débat la question de la responsabilité des acteurs impliqués dans l’exploitation minière à Siguiri. Son intervention met en lumière les enjeux environnementaux, sanitaires et administratifs liés à cette activité, tout en appelant à des réponses durables pour préserver les ressources naturelles et protéger les populations guinéennes.

items.title: Carrick the fall guy for deeper problems at Man Utd – Report
items.description: Michael Carrick is the latest in a long line of managers to be sacked by Manchester United as they struggle to recapture former glories, but their problems run far deeper than the dugout. For the first time in 40 years, the 20-time English champions find themselves in the Premier League relegation zone at this stage of the season. Carrick was handed the job on a permanent basis fewer than six months ago after revitalising the team following the acrimonious departure of Ruben Amorim in January. Under the 45-year-old, then operating as interim boss, United finished third in the Premier League, securing a return to the Champions League after two seasons away. But the optimism quickly vanished at the start of this season and for the third consecutive campaign, woeful results have forced United into a mid-season managerial change. The Red Devils have won just three of their opening 15 games in all competitions. Carrick joins David Moyes, Louis van Gaal, Jose Mourinho, Ole Gunnar Solskjaer, Erik ten Hag and Amorim among the managers who have struggled to arrest United’s overall decline, despite the occasional trophy, since Alex Ferguson retired in 2013. The Scot stepped down after collecting his 13th Premier League winner’s medal, at the end of a period of dominance in English football and European success. Now United, almost unbelievably, find themselves in a battle just to stay in the English top flight, where they have been ever-present for more than 50 years. USA head coach Mauricio Pochettino — the hot favourite to replace Carrick — faces the task of uniting a deeply divided club on and off the pitch. United captain Bruno Fernandes was dropped last month after he criticised Carrick’s tactics following a 4-1 humbling by Como. And defender Lisandro Martinez took a public swipe at the United hierarchy for not doing more to strengthen the squad in the summer transfer window. Carrick’s role as a player in the glory days under Ferguson meant he retained support among the fanbase despite a string of substandard displays. – Blame game – The anger of the supporters is instead firmly directed towards the club’s owners, whom they hold responsible for overseeing United’s slide. Despite fierce and persistent protests over two decades, the US-based Glazer family still hold a majority stake in the club, which Malcolm Glazer bought via a leveraged takeover in 2005, saddling United with huge debts. Any hopes that the arrival of British billionaire Jim Ratcliffe as a minority owner in 2024 would signal a new dawn have since faded. Ratcliffe, founder and chairman of industrial giant INEOS, has overseen cost-cutting measures, including widespread redundancies, and hiked up ticket prices, but the club’s debt has still soared above £1.1 billion ($1.46 billion). Former United captain Gary Neville has lamented the “inept” ownership and leadership of his boyhood club. The Manchester United Supporters’ Trust (MUST), meanwhile, issued a statement following Carrick’s dismissal pinning the blame for poor results firmly on the ownership. “The Glazers’ debt-funded takeover continues to burden the club,” MUST said in a statement. “When INEOS came in they promised sporting excellence, but yet with repeated changes in football leadership we have seen anything but. “It is time for the owners to explain themselves and show some accountability.” Another huge issue is the future of Old Trafford. The biggest club stadium in English football now looks tired and outdated. Plans for a new 100,000-seater venue have not been universally welcomed and it remains unclear how that project would be financed. “We don’t want a new stadium, we want new owners,” read a banner at Sunday’s chaotic 4-4 draw at home to Aston Villa, which proved to be Carrick’s last game in charge. “You can keep changing the manager and thinking that’s going to be the answer,” said Neville. “(If) you’ve not got leadership that is strong right through the spine of the football club you will fail.” United last dropped out of the top division in 1974. They cannot afford to let it happen again. The post Carrick the fall guy for deeper problems at Man Utd – Report appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Victoire de Lula au Brésil. Au coeur d’une « remontada » populaire
items.description: À télécharger Lire la note (PDF) Une douche froide. Voici la meilleure expression pour expliquer le résultat du premier tour des élections brésiliennes du 4 octobre 2026 pour une bonne partie du peuple brésilien. Alors que tous les sondages donnaient une petite avance au président Lula sur son rival, Flávio Bolsonaro, fils aîné de l’ancien président d’extrême droite battu en 2022 par Lula lui-même et actuellement en résidence surveillée pour une tentative de coup d’État, Lula arrive en deuxième position avec deux points d’écart, obtenant 45 % des voix contre 47 %. Les autres candidats, plutôt de droite, ont obtenu des résultats peu significatifs. Le Parti libéral, l’extrême droite conservatrice, avait remporté 121 sièges de députés sur 513, ainsi que 19 sièges de sénateurs sur les 54 soumis au suffrage universel (pour un total de 29 sur 81), et une majorité de postes de gouverneur des États de la fédération. Aucun sondage n’avait non plus prévu ces résultats. Une autre donnée semblait échapper aux sondages : la domination massive de l’extrême droite sur les réseaux sociaux. S’ils semblaient moins présents dans la rue, ses partisans dominaient la communication sur tous les réseaux, qu’il s’agisse de X, Instagram, Facebook ou WhatsApp. À tel point que la campagne de Lula a déposé une plainte contre la Big Tech Meta, accusée de favoriser expressément son rival dans la diffusion des contenus. La situation défavorable au lendemain du premier tour montrait qu’il fallait changer radicalement l’orientation de la campagne. L’article Victoire de Lula au Brésil. Au coeur d'une « remontada » populaire est apparu en premier sur IRIS .

items.title: Power shutdown at Dhabeji to cause Karachi-wide water shortage tomorrow
items.description: KARACHI: The city will face a shortfall of around 130 million gallons of water per day (MGD) on Friday (tomorrow) as K-Electric (KE) and the Karachi Water and Sewerage Corporation (KWSC) carry out annual maintenance work at the Dhabeji Pumping Station. The city normally receives around 650 MGD but supply will drop to 520 MGD during the shutdown. According to a KWSC spokesperson, KE has formally notified the water utility of the scheduled power shutdown. “Electricity supply to Dhabeji Grid Station will remain suspended on Nov 13 for annual maintenance,” he said. The power shutdown will last 14 hours, from 10am to midnight on Nov 13. During this period, nine of the 21 pumps at Dhabeji will remain non-operational, the spokesperson added. He said the power outage would affect water supply to Landhi, Korangi, Malir, Shah Faisal, Gulshan, Clifton, Saddar and Lyari. Supplies to various towns including Jinnah, Chanesar, Liaquatabad and North Karachi would also be affected. Water supply to Nazimabad and Gulberg towns would be partially disrupted while the Landhi and Sherpao hydrants would remain closed during the shutdown. The spokesperson said that once KE completed its annual maintenance, six of the nine affected pumps at Dhabeji would be made operational. With these pumps back in service, water supply would return to normal in all affected areas except Landhi, Korangi, Malir and Shah Faisal. He added that the KWSC’s annual maintenance work would continue for another 22 hours after KE’s shutdown ended. During this period, only three pumps at Dhabeji would remain non-operational, resulting in a partial disruption of water supply to Landhi, Korangi, Malir and Shah Faisal. Meanwhile, a KE spokesperson said the scheduled maintenance shutdown at Dhabeji Grid Station would take place on Friday and that advance notice had been shared with the KWSC. The work would include testing and servicing the grid’s power transformer, as well as testing and maintaining its vacuum circuit breaker (VCB) switches. Technical faults would also be addressed while cleaning the relevant substation, the spokesperson added. The maintenance activities are essential to ensuring a continuous and reliable power supply, he said. Published in Dawn, November 12th, 2026

items.title: Manhyia South MP allowed to retrieve passport as court varies bail terms
items.description: The High Court in Accra has varied the bail conditions of Manhyia South Member of Parliament, Nana Agyei Baffour Awuah, allowing him to retrieve his passport from the court registry. The Commercial Court 5 Division granted the application on Thursday, November 12, 2026, during proceedings in the MP’s trial over allegations of causing financial loss to the state and money laundering. His lawyer, Samuel Atta Akyea, urged the court to approve the request, arguing that his client had no intention of fleeing the country. He also cited parliamentary rules requiring MPs to attend sittings, warning that prolonged absence without the Speaker’s written permission and a reasonable explanation could put the legislator’s seat at risk. Article 97(1)(c) of the 1992 Constitution provides that an MP shall vacate their seat if they are absent from 15 sittings of Parliament without the Speaker’s written permission and are unable to offer a reasonable explanation to the Privileges Committee. Deputy Attorney-General Dr Justice Srem-Sai, who represented the prosecution, did not oppose the application. Justice Charity Akosua Asem subsequently approved the request, removing the requirement for the MP’s passport to remain in the custody of the court registry. Mr Awuah is standing trial over allegations relating to his handling of a legal case involving SIC Life Savings and Loans Company Limited. He faces charges of conspiracy to commit a crime, specifically the intentional dissipation of public funds, intentionally causing financial loss to a public body, and money laundering. The MP voluntarily surrendered to the Economic and Organised Crime Office (EOCO) on October 1, 2026, following a High Court warrant issued on September 30, 2026. Although the latest ruling allows him to retrieve his passport, he remains subject to the other bail conditions. The trial is expected to continue.

items.title: Health Ministry warns public against fraudulent Mercy Ships fundraising campaign
items.description: The Ministry of Health has warned the public against a fraudulent fundraising campaign being aired on some Ghanaian television stations, which falsely solicits money from people seeking surgical treatment through Mercy Ships. In a press release dated November 10, 2026, the Ministry said the campaign, featuring an organisation identified as the “HELP Save LIFE Foundation”, was requesting financial contributions through an MTN Mobile Money account. It stressed that the fundraising campaign was not affiliated with, authorised by or endorsed by Mercy Ships. The Ministry explained that Mercy Ships International, an organisation that provides free surgical care and medical education across Africa, currently has its hospital vessel, The Global Mercy, docked at the Tema Port. The vessel is expected to provide free surgeries to more than 2,500 Ghanaians over a 10-month period ending in June 2027. According to the Ministry, patients scheduled for treatment were identified and pre-screened before the vessel’s arrival through a coordinated process involving Mercy Ships and the Ministry, based on established medical and eligibility criteria. It added that the hospital vessel was currently operating at full capacity and was not accepting additional patients for the ongoing field service. The Ministry cautioned that payments or registrations through third parties would not guarantee access to treatment, emphasising that all medical services provided by Mercy Ships were entirely free. It urged the public not to make payments, share personal or financial information or engage with individuals claiming they could facilitate access to the services. The Ministry has encouraged anyone who suspects fraudulent activity to report it to the Cyber Security Authority through call or SMS to 292, or by email at report@csa.gov.gh. Suspected incidents may also be reported to the nearest police station, MTN Ghana through its 100 customer service line, or Mercy Ships through its official communication channels. The Ministry described the exploitation of vulnerable patients and their families through fraudulent schemes as unacceptable and urged the public to rely only on official communication channels for information on Mercy Ships services and patient access.

items.title: Ouverture du marché à terme au Maroc : la BCP et Upline Securities obtiennent leurs agréments
items.description: La BCP (Banque Centrale Populaire) et sa filiale Upline Securities annoncent l’obtention de leurs agréments dans le cadre de l’ouverture du marché à terme au Maroc. À l’occasion du lancement du marché à terme au Maroc, une étape structurante dans le développement et la modernisation du marché des capitaux national, la BCP (Banque Centrale Populaire) et sa filiale Upline Securities annoncent l’obtention de leurs agréments auprès des autorités compétentes. Dans le cadre de cette évolution, la BCP s’est vu accorder les agréments de compensateur et de négociateur, qui lui permettent d’intervenir sur l’ensemble de la chaîne de valeur des opérations sur instruments dérivés, avec un rôle structurant dans la compensation (déléguée à notre filiale BCP Securities Services) et une capacité élargie d’accompagnement des intervenants de marché. De son côté, Upline Securities a obtenu l’agrément de négociateur, renforçant ainsi son positionnement en tant qu’acteur clé de l’intermédiation sur les marchés financiers. L’attribution de ces agréments s’inscrit dans la dynamique d’accompagnement du lancement du marché à terme, conçu pour offrir aux investisseurs des outils de couverture et de gestion des risques, tout en contribuant à l’amélioration de la liquidité et de l’efficience du marché financier marocain. Cette avancée marque une nouvelle étape dans le développement des services bancaires du Groupe et de ses filiales. Elle s’inscrit dans la continuité de sa stratégie visant à renforcer son expertise sur les marchés de capitaux et à offrir un accompagnement de proximité à ses clients, dans un environnement en pleine transformation, en mettant à leur disposition des instruments modernes adaptés à leurs besoins et alignés sur les standards internationaux. The post Ouverture du marché à terme au Maroc : la BCP et Upline Securities obtiennent leurs agréments appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: When the outrage dies, who remembers the victims? – The Obuasi SHTS case and our troubling habit of forgetting the people behind the headlines
items.description: The speed at which victims of sexual abuse, especially children, can become less central to the public discussion of their experience once the outrage dies away is deeply troubling. A common pattern exists in the manner in which we typically respond to unsettling stories in our region. A tragedy occurs, an inquiry reveals some unpleasant truth, social media erupts with outrage, high-profile individuals offer their condolences and opinions, and citizens call for accountability. Depending on the degree of disturbance created by the story, national discussion can dominate public discourse anywhere from a couple of days to several weeks. Once another story begins to gather attention, public focus will shift, and the individuals at the center of the original scandal will be left to deal with the consequences of the scandal, usually without the same amount of public outcry that originally surrounded them. This is a pattern that should worry us. The recent allegations of sexual abuse involving female students at Obuasi Senior High Technical School (SHTS) have once again brought questions of child protection, institutional accountability and the safety of girls into Ghana’s national conversation. Following an investigation by Joy News, the case prompted public outrage, government intervention and renewed scrutiny of the Ghana Education Service and its handling of complaints. The headmaster has been interdicted pending investigations, while the education ministry has announced support for 19 students identified in connection with the allegations, including psychological counselling, medical care and academic assistance. Each of these actions is an essential measure. However, I am currently focused on a larger question. What happens when the public stops paying attention? Because the uncomfortable reality is that the consequences of abuse do not disappear when a story stops trending. The fear, trauma, disruption to education, and struggle to rebuild a sense of safety do not operate on the same timeline as public outrage. We remember the story, but do we remember the people? One of the most troubling aspects of our response to humanitarian and social issues is how easily we become invested in the story but lose sight of the people experiencing it. We remember the headline and the outrage and debate who should be held responsible. Yet how often do we return to ask whether the people affected are actually receiving the support they were promised? In cases involving sexual abuse, particularly where children are concerned, the need for sustained attention is even greater. The immediate public reaction may create pressure for intervention, but recovery and protection require much more than a moment of national sympathy. For the students at Obuasi, the questions above should not conclude with an announcement stating that counseling and medical support will be provided. Will these services be provided? Will their academic development be supported? Will they be free from intimidation, victim-blaming, and unwanted public attention, and will their identities remain protected? Each of these points represents a critical component of what a meaningful response should look like. We must be careful not to assume that an announcement means an intervention has been fully implemented. Equally, we should not assume that nothing is being done simply because the public has not received every detail. What we need is appropriate transparency, sustained monitoring and evidence that the commitments made are translating into actual support. This problem extends beyond Obuasi and beyond sexual abuse cases. Disturbing cases of violence against women, child exploitation, among others occasionally generate sufficient national interest to warrant national attention. We show outrage over such cases and declare our solidarity with victims. Yet we frequently lack the ability to sustain our outrage beyond the initial controversy. Consider the reported sexual abuse of a 14-year-old autistic student at Bolgatanga Girls’ Senior High School, which also reignited conversations about safeguarding and the vulnerability of children within educational institutions in September 2026. Different cases have different circumstances, and should be investigated on their own evidence. However, recurring concerns about the protection of students should prompt us to examine whether our responses are producing lasting improvements or simply reacting to each new incident. We cannot keep treating every disturbing revelation as an isolated controversy when similar questions about reporting, institutional responsibility and student safety continue to arise. The problem with reactive advocacy is that it places enormous attention on the moment of exposure but often insufficient attention on what follows. We become passionate about demanding action when a story is fresh, but less consistent in monitoring whether that action has happened. And when public attention disappears, the pressure on institutions to demonstrate progress can disappear with it. Accountability should never depend upon public pressure. One of the most significant lessons learned from the Obuasi case is that children should never suffer as a result of whether or not an investigative journalist exposes a problem or whether enough public outrage exists to compel action from authorities. Schools and educational authorities have responsibilities that exist regardless of whether or not the public is watching. We must learn to stay As a young woman involved in humanitarian work and women’s rights advocacy, I believe one of the largest challenges facing social advocacy is not always getting people to care. Sometimes it is getting them to continue caring long after the initial emotional response has passed. There is a difference between feeling sorry for someone and committing to support them, a difference between demanding justice and ensuring that justice was pursued, and there is a difference between sharing a story and being responsible for ensuring that the issues raised by that story were not forgotten. This is why journalists, civil society organisations, child protection advocates, women’s rights groups and concerned citizens must continue asking questions long after the initial headlines disappear. We must follow up on investigations, monitor institutional commitments, demand appropriate updates and keep the needs of affected people in public conversation without compromising their privacy or dignity. Our advocacy must also extend beyond individual controversies to the policies, safeguards and social attitudes that allow harm to occur in the first place. The students of Obuasi and every victim of sexual abuse deserve more than just a moment of national sympathy. They deserve protection, support, a credible process for establishing the facts and an educational environment in which their safety is taken seriously. The headmaster is equally entitled to due process, and allegations must be established through the appropriate legal processes. Neither principle should be sacrificed. Ultimately, the measure of our concern cannot be how loudly we react when a disturbing story breaks. It must also be how consistently we demand answers when the excitement has passed. The people behind our headlines do not get to move on simply because the rest of us have. If our outrage disappears before their painful experience had been addressed and prior to any accountability having been secured, then perhaps we must begin to question whether or not our outrage was worth anything.

items.title: Haho/108ème anniversaire de l’armistice de la 1ère guerre mondiale : dépôts de gerbes au mémorial à Wahala
items.description: Notsè, 12 nov. (ATOP) – Le 108 ème anniversaire de l’armistice de la 1 ère guerre mondiale a été commémoré le mercredi 11 novembre par des dépôts de gerbes au mémorial des illustres disparus à Wahala dans la commune Haho 4. La cérémonie a connu la présence, entre autres, de l’ambassadeur du Ghana, Gorge Nfojol, des chargés d’affaires de l’ambassade d’Allemagne, Johannes Klotz, de l’attaché de la Centrafrique, lieutenant Yakende Emèlie Prisca et du chargé du secrétariat général et de communication Lawson- Domoloma André Lionel. Le chargé de mission de la Grande Bretagne, William Turner, ceux d’affaires de l’Union Européenne, Niccolò Maracchi et du Sénégal, Ciré Ba, et le maire adjoint de la commune Haho 4 ont assisté également à cet événement. Après l’exécution des hymnes nationaux du Togo, de la Grande Bretagne et de la France, ces personnalités ont déposé des gerbes au mémorial de Walala en mémoire des africains et européens ayant sacrifié leurs vies pour la liberté et la justice. Le chargé d’affaires de l’ambassade de France, Frédéric Lopez a rendu hommage aux illustres disparus. Selon lui, le 11 novembre marque une commémoration nationale et internationale de la victoire de la paix, après l’armistice de 1918. Devant les tombes des illustres disparus Les autorités Pour le préfet de Haho, Colonel Gnakou Alowegnim, cette commémoration est un devoir de mémoire et un engagement collectif à la préservation de l’histoire commune. D’après lui, le mémorial de Wahala dans la commune Haho 4 rappelle un épisode douloureux de l’histoire marquée par la bataille de Rah en 1914 au cours de laquelle des soldats ont perdu la vie. La commémoration a été aussi un cadre d’échange et d’appropriation de l’histoire par les élèves des lycées français, Cours lumière, British school et le lycée de Wahala. Ces derniers ont découvert les auteurs et récits des illustres disparus de la guerre de 1914. ATOP/YM/AR/BV

items.title: Nepra notifies Rs25.30 per unit revised special industrial tariff despite concerns
items.description: ISLAMABAD: The National Electric Power Regulatory Authority (Nepra) on Thursday notified a Rs25.30 per unit revised incremental consumption package (ICP) for industry and agriculture to encourage higher consumption. The order comes despite dissenting notes from two of its four members on Friday, when the authority made the announcement, and protest from industrial consumers. The revised ICP replaces the previous rate of Rs22.98 per unit, which was introduced in December last year for six months to encourage industrial and agricultural consumers to consume more electricity at a marginal cost of Rs22.98 on additional consumption, instead of their normal rate that stood at Rs34.50 per unit last month. In a statutory regulatory order (SRO) issued in the Gazette of Pakistan, Nepra said it notified the authority’s decision dated Nov 6, along with dissent notes from Nepra members Amina Ahmed and Maqsood Anwar Khan; as well as an additional note and casting vote of Nepra Chairman Waseem Mukhtar in the matter of the “semi-annual review of the ICP for industrial and agricultural electricity consumers of XWDiscos and K-Electric”. The decision, opposed by the industrial sector, is likely to have a negative impact on all electricity consumers, including those served by K-Electric and other distribution companies (Discos). Industrial consumers complained that the Rs25.30 per unit revised ICP — against the actual marginal cost of Rs31.83 or Rs29.65 per unit calculated by Nepra —resulted in higher monthly fuel cost adjustments (FCAs) and burdened all consumer categories across the country. This was despite the fact that the ICP announced in December last year on the prime minister’s instructions was based on the commitment that any additional costs arising from the package would remain ring-fenced, and that the difference between consumer-end tariff and ICP would not be shifted to any other consumer category except the ICP beneficiaries , the consumers said. Nepra members’ observations In the determination issued on the ICP last Friday, all four members of the regulator unanimously held the Power Division and its subordinate entities responsible for failing to fulfil their legal obligations within the prescribed timelines, pushing Nepra into an unprecedented deadlock and potentially increasing costs for electricity consumers across the country. Nepra chairman Mukhtar fully endorsed the written arguments and positions taken by the dissenting members, but subsequently exercised his special casting vote to approve the revised rate of Rs25.30 per unit. The authority was divided 2-2 on the matter. Member (Tariff and Finance) Amina Ahmed and Member (Development) Maqsood Anwar, in a joint dissenting note, had maintained that even the proposed revised rate of Rs25.30 per unit was a “random number” unsupported by evidence. They said that Nepra’s own institutional calculations put the marginal cost at Rs31.83 per unit. “The revised incremental rate of Rs25.30 per unit proposed by the Ministry of Energy (MoE), and allowed by the honourable chairman and Member (Law), is based on the generation mix apparently assumed at the design stage of the package, with updated fuel prices,” the two members observed. They called for the immediate suspension of the ICP until authentic data became available. The dissenting members argued that compliance with the federal cabinet’s decision and Nepra’s own directives required a reassessment of the existing rate of Rs22.98 per unit to determine whether it should be retained, revised or suspended. However, this exercise had not been carried out, resulting in the continuation of the package at a rate below the actual cost of supplying incremental electricity. “The resulting misalignment has had implications for consumers in two ways. First, to the extent incremental consumption increased the system’s average fuel cost, the resulting impact was recovered from all consumers through the FCA mechanism. Second, because incremental units are excluded from quarterly tariff adjustments, the exclusion of such units increases the quarterly adjustment borne by consumers not availing the package,” they said. They questioned how a package based on the principle of cost-reflectivity could continue without a validated cost-reflective rate, arguing that since the alternative rate had no credible link with the actual marginal cost, continuation of the package was no longer justified. They said other consumers should not be made to bear the cost of a review that the MoE was required to submit five months ago but had yet to provide. In his casting vote, Mukhtar observed that the dissenting members’ conclusions “need serious consideration”. However, he said suspending the package at this stage would not be appropriate and that the MoE should be given another opportunity to provide the information repeatedly sought by the regulator, including in its latest determination. All four members agreed that the Power Division was required to submit revised calculations six months ago but had failed to do so, despite repeated reminders from Nepra. They also regretted that the ministry had not responded adequately to the questions and queries raised by the regulator. “The marginal price, in proper form, was not provided to the regulator by either the Independent System and Market Operator (ISMO) or the Power Planning and Monitoring Company (PPMC), which were duty-bound to do so. Since the ISP is a flagship project of the ministry, it should give due consideration to the observations of Nepra and the lack of inter-agency coordination among the entities working under the ministry,” the members observed. The determination also sets deadlines for the relevant entities to provide the required information. The four members warned that failure to meet these deadlines could lead to an adverse outcome in the review of the programme, including its suspension or termination. “Furthermore, any entity that fails to provide the required information within the stipulated timeline shall lead to initiation of legal proceedings under the applicable legal framework,” they stated. Explaining his decision, the chairman said: “I hereby exercise, in due and faithful discharge of the functions of the authority, my second and casting vote envisaged and entrusted to me under the Nepra Act in favour of the first opinion, thereby breaking the deadlock in relation to the aforesaid issues. Accordingly, the first opinion constitutes the order of the authority.”

items.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigns after tech giant rocked by second affair allegation
items.description: Jensen Huang has resigned as chief executive of Nvidia, the artificial intelligence chipmaker he co-founded, following reports of two extramarital relationships, including one involving a woman suspected by US intelligence officials of having links to Chinese intelligence. Nvidia’s board of directors announced on Thursday, November 12, that Huang’s departure as CEO and board member would take immediate effect. His resignation follows an investigation launched by the company after reports that he had an intimate relationship with a woman identified in media reports as Alice Huang, a former executive of Singapore-based data centre company Megaspeed International. US intelligence officials reportedly suspected Alice Huang of working for Chinese intelligence, raising concerns about whether the relationship could have exposed sensitive company or national security information. Nvidia’s board had earlier said it had no reason to believe that national security or company secrets had been compromised. The development follows a report by The New York Times on Wednesday that Huang had also been involved in an intimate relationship with Kimberly Powell, Nvidia’s vice-president of healthcare. The newspaper cited five people who had worked at the company. Huang had admitted to being unfaithful to his wife in a message to Nvidia employees, apologising to his family and colleagues. “I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry,” he said. National security concerns The allegations had drawn attention from US lawmakers, with Democrats preparing to investigate the circumstances surrounding Huang’s relationship with the woman suspected of espionage and the extent of President Donald Trump’s knowledge of the alleged Chinese intelligence operation. The controversy has also renewed scrutiny of Nvidia’s business dealings with China, particularly the sale of advanced artificial intelligence chips amid US efforts to restrict Beijing’s access to sensitive technology. Nvidia’s board had said its investigation would examine the available information, while maintaining that it had no reason to believe that company secrets or national security had been compromised. items.title: Power expires. Friendships shouldn’t
items.description: By Kwame Sowu There is something profoundly disturbing about people who occupy fixed-term public offices or privileged corporate positions and suddenly develop amnesia about the relationships that existed before their appointments. The phone numbers remain, but the friendships disappear. People who once shared ideas, dreams and ambitions are suddenly considered too ordinary to associate with. Friends in entrepreneurship are ignored. Calls go unanswered. Requests for modest assistance are treated as personal inconveniences. Some even become unnecessarily arrogant, as though their appointments have permanently elevated them into another species. How foolish! Have we not learnt that appointments end? Governments change. Retirement comes. Contracts expire. Political fortunes reverse. The same corridors of power that once welcomed you will eventually become unfamiliar territory. The security detail disappears, the official vehicle is withdrawn, the privileges evaporate and suddenly, the world becomes remarkably quiet. Then comes the desperate scrolling through old contacts. You begin searching for people whose calls you once ignored. You remember friends whose businesses you could have helped nurture. You suddenly rediscover relationships you abandoned when you thought your position made you important. My intention is not to curse anyone. It is a caution. Never confuse the office you occupy with the person you are. An appointment is a temporary privilege, not a personal inheritance. The position is yours only for a season. The people you meet along the way are part of your permanent journey. If you have friends building businesses, creating jobs and developing ideas, help them where you legitimately can. Open doors. Share opportunities. Make introductions. Support enterprise. Do so ethically, transparently and without abusing your office. You do not have to compromise your integrity to be a good friend. One day, you will leave that office. When you do, may you leave with your dignity intact, your conscience clear and enough genuine friendships to remind you that you mattered beyond your title. Power is borrowed. Humanity is permanent.

items.title: Air Algérie ouvre les réservations pour l’été 2027 : Alger – Paris dès 22.929 DA en juillet
items.description: Air Algérie a déjà ouvert les réservations pour la saison estivale 2027. Les places et vols disponibles à l’international sont consultables sur la plateforme en ligne officielle de la compagnie aérienne algérienne, alors qu'on est encore dans la première moitié de novembre. Les offres sont intéressantes sur certaines destinations, très chères sur d'autres. À noter que l’ouverture des réservations n’a fait l’objet d'aucune annonce officielle de la part de la compagnie. Les émigrés et les résidents peuvent réserver dès maintenant pour l’été sur Air Algérie Ce qui est certain, c’est que, comme chaque été, ce sera le rush sur les vols d’Air Algérie lors de la saison estivale prochaine, notamment sur les liaisons de et vers la France. La demande est boostée par les départs en vacances vers leur pays d’origine des membres de la forte communauté algérienne établie en France. Pour leur faciliter les choses et leur permettre d'organiser à l’avance leurs congés et leurs voyages, Air Algérie a ouvert les réservations plusieurs mois à l’avance, sachant que la saison estivale commence en juin et atteint son pic en juillet et août. Les réservations sur les vols de et vers le Canada sont aussi ouvertes, pour les mêmes raisons. Des prix très élevés au départ de la France, intéressants dans le sens inverse Sans surprise, les prix des vols à partir des aéroports français vers les villes algériennes sont très élevés. En juin, le billet sur un vol de Paris-Charles-de-Gaulle à destination de l’aéroport international d’Alger, en aller-retour, est proposé à 403,68 euros. Le billet sur la même ligne atteint 546,68 euros en juillet et 630,68 euros en août, selon le site spécialiste Voyages & Diaspora . Le billet le plus cher entre la France et l’Algérie, soit 657,34 euros, est proposé sur un vol Lille-Alger au mois d'août. Sur Marseille-Alger, les prix vont de 297,95 euros en juin à 464,95 euros en août. En revanche, les prix proposés sur les vols au départ de l’Algérie sont intéressants. Par exemple, Alger-Paris est à seulement 22 929 DA en juillet, soit 151,18 euros au taux de change officiel, et nettement moins au taux parallèle (83 euros). À partir du Canada, le billet aller-retour Montréal-Alger en juillet coûte 974,02 euros. L’article Air Algérie ouvre les réservations pour l’été 2027 : Alger – Paris dès 22.929 DA en juillet est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: Exploitation minière illégale : 132 étrangers frappés au portefeuille, 2 640 milliards fg d’amendes cumulées
items.description: Le tribunal de première instance de Kankan a rendu son verdict concernant une partie des 194 personnes interpellées dans les préfectures de Kérouané et de Siguiri pour des faits présumés d’exploitation minière illégale, de dégradation de l’environnement et d’exercice d’activités minières sans autorisation. Au total, 132 ressortissants étrangers ont été condamnés à un an d’emprisonnement ferme et à une amende de 20 milliards de francs guinéens chacun. Le sort des 29 prévenus guinéens reste, quant à lui, en suspens, leurs audiences étant toujours en cours. Ouvert le mercredi 11 novembre 2026, ce procès se tient dans les locaux de la Cour d’appel de Kankan, où les audiences ont été délocalisées en raison du nombre élevé de prévenus. Les débats sont répartis entre les salles d’audience A et B, sous la conduite du tribunal de première instance de Kankan. Dans le volet consacré aux mineurs, le tribunal a statué sur le cas de 33 personnes. Six ont été relaxées, tandis que les 27 autres ont écopé de dix jours de détention et d’une amende de 200 000 francs guinéens chacune. Le cas d’un enfant âgé de moins de 13 ans a également été examiné, celui-ci n’étant pas pénalement responsable dans les mêmes conditions que les autres prévenus. Pour les 132 ressortissants étrangers, la juridiction a prononcé une peine d’un an d’emprisonnement ferme, assortie d’une amende de 20 milliards de francs guinéens par personne, en application de l’article 178 du Code de l’environnement guinéen. Le tribunal a également ordonné leur expulsion du territoire national et leur a interdit tout séjour en Guinée pendant une durée de dix ans. En revanche, les 29 Guinéens poursuivis dans cette même affaire, parmi lesquels figurent des hommes et des femmes, attendent toujours leur jugement. Les audiences les concernant se poursuivent et la décision du tribunal n’était pas encore connue au moment de la rédaction de cet article. Les prévenus sont poursuivis pour »exploitation minière illégale, dégradation de l’environnement et exercice d’activités minières sans autorisation ».

items.title: Ogou : atelier d’orientation de SOS villages d’enfants sur le gatekeeping
items.description: Atakpamé, 12 nov. (ATOP) – Un atelier d’orientation des partenaires sur la prévention des mauvais placements (Gatekeeping) et les directives régissant la prise en charge alternative des enfants se tient les 12 et 13 novembre à Atakpamé. Organisée par le programme Atakpamé de SOS Villages d’Enfants Togo, cette rencontre réunit les acteurs de la chaîne de protection de l’enfance, notamment les services de l’Action sociale, la justice, les forces de l’ordre et de sécurité, les autorités traditionnelles ainsi que les leaders religieux. L’objectif de cet atelier est d’orienter les partenaires sur les documents réglementant la prise en charge alternative et de dresser le bilan annuel des activités menées par l’organisation. Les travaux visent à renforcer la compréhension des participants sur le concept du Gatekeeping, à clarifier les critères d’éligibilité et le processus de gestion des cas, à présenter les résultats de prise en charge obtenus en 2025, et à recueillir des propositions pour améliorer la protection dans la région des Plateaux. Au cours des assises, les échanges vont porter sur les politiques stratégiques telles que le « SOS Care Promise », les principes d’adéquation et de nécessité conformes aux Lignes directrices des Nations unies, ainsi que le mécanisme de référencement des enfants vulnérables. Les travaux en groupes et en plénière permettront également d’analyser les défis et difficultés rencontrés sur le terrain afin de formuler des recommandations opérationnelles. Selon le bilan de l’année 2025 présenté aux partenaires, le programme Atakpamé a accompagné au total 130 enfants à travers ses quatre options de prise en charge. Il s’agit de 72 enfants accueillis dans les maisons de transit pour une sécurisation d’urgence, 40 enfants pris en charge au sein des familles SOS intégrées en communauté, 12 enfants placés dans des familles d’accueil civiles, et 6 jeunes accompagnés en habitat semi-encadré dans le cadre d’un processus d’autonomisation. L’organisation ambitionne d’optimiser la détection précoce des cas et la pertinence des référencements afin de garantir que chaque enfant orienté corresponde strictement à la cible du programme et bénéficie d’un accompagnement vers la réinsertion ou l’autonomie. Le chef division alphabétisation et éducation non formelle à la direction régionale des Solidarités Plateaux, Aglolou Kofi, a rappelé l’importance de respecter les principes d’adéquation et de nécessité de la prise en charge, conformément aux normes internationales. Il a souligné qu’il est indispensable de renouveler les connaissances des partenaires en renforçant les capacités des différentes parties prenantes en vue d’améliorer les pratiques sur le terrain. M. Aaron Kagnala Bassanga, coordonnateur local de la prise en charge alternative de SOS Villages d’Enfants a insisté sur le rôle déterminant des partenaires dans le dispositif de protection. « Les partenaires détectent et identifient en première ligne les enfants en situation de vulnérabilité urgente, nous attendons d’eux une réaction proactive et une même compréhension de la cible afin d’assurer une prise en charge de qualité », a-t-il indiqué. ATOP/KKT/MG/BV

items.title: Maroc : Le gouvernement suspend les nouvelles autorisations d’exportation de tomates, d’oignons et de pommes de terre
items.description: Fatima Zahra El Mansouri, cheffe du gouvernement, a affirmé que la protection du pouvoir d’achat des citoyens demeurait la première priorité de l’Exécutif. Elle a annoncé la suspension temporaire de l’octroi de nouvelles autorisations d’exportation de tomates, d’oignons et de pommes de terre, afin de préserver l’approvisionnement du marché national. Lors de la réunion hebdomadaire du Conseil de gouvernement, tenue jeudi, Mansouri a indiqué que l’Exécutif avait mis en place une commission interministérielle chargée de suivre l’évolution des prix. Elle a également annoncé la poursuite du soutien exceptionnel accordé aux professionnels du transport routier, dans le cadre des mesures destinées à protéger le pouvoir d’achat des citoyens. Selon un communiqué du ministère de l’Aménagement du territoire national, de l’Urbanisme, de l’Habitat et de la Politique de la ville, porte-parole du gouvernement, elle a souligné que la lutte contre la hausse des prix des produits alimentaires et des carburants exigeait de garantir l’approvisionnement des marchés et de combattre la spéculation et les pratiques monopolistiques. Dans le même contexte, Mansouri a annoncé la décision de suspendre temporairement l’octroi de nouvelles autorisations d’exportation de tomates, d’oignons et de pommes de terre. Elle a insisté sur la nécessité de protéger le marché national, tout en préservant les intérêts des agriculteurs et des partenaires du Maroc sur le continent africain. Elle a également souligné l’importance d’un suivi quotidien des prix et d’une préparation anticipée du mois de Ramadan. Par ailleurs, les membres du Conseil de gouvernement ont examiné et adopté un projet de loi et trois projets de décrets. Le projet de loi n° 06.25 porte sur la transformation de l’Office national des aéroports (ONDA) en société anonyme. Cette opération s’inscrit dans le cadre des dispositions de la loi-cadre n° 21.50 relative à la réforme des établissements et entreprises publics, tout en tenant compte de la loi n° 82.20 portant création de l’Agence nationale de gestion stratégique des participations de l’État et de suivi des performances des établissements et entreprises publics. Ce projet vise à accompagner l’importance stratégique des aéroports, considérés comme un pilier essentiel du développement économique, notamment dans le secteur touristique, et à répondre aux défis auxquels fait face le transport aérien. Il prévoit ainsi une amélioration de la gouvernance des infrastructures aéroportuaires, conformément aux normes internationales en matière de sécurité, d’efficacité et de compétitivité. La transformation de l’ONDA, d’établissement public en société anonyme, repose sur la création d’une société dénommée « Aéroports du Maroc SA », chargée de gérer la navigation aérienne et le domaine public aéroportuaire pour le compte de l’État. Elle prévoit également l’octroi, par le biais de conventions spécifiques, de concessions de gestion et d’exploitation des aéroports désignés par la société à ses filiales, ainsi que la création d’une filiale chargée de gérer les titres de participation dans les filiales aéroportuaires. Le Conseil a également adopté le projet de décret n° 2.26.592 complétant le décret n° 2.17.226 du 29 juin 2017, relatif à la liste des diplômes et certificats préparés et délivrés par les instituts et établissements relevant de l’Université Al Quaraouiyine. Ce texte vise à intégrer le cycle de doctorat, créé au sein de l’Institut Mohammed VI des lectures et études coraniques relevant de l’Université Al Quaraouiyine, à la liste des diplômes et certificats préparés et délivrés par les établissements et instituts de cette université. Le Conseil a par ailleurs approuvé le projet de décret n° 2.26.526 portant adoption de mesures réglementaires au profit de certaines catégories de fonctionnaires du ministère de la Justice. Ce texte vise à permettre à des catégories d’agents, notamment ceux mis à la disposition du ministère ou placés en position de détachement auprès de celui-ci, de bénéficier de la prime de rendement accordée à plusieurs catégories de fonctionnaires du département. Enfin, le Conseil a adopté le projet de décret n° 2.26.838 modifiant le décret n° 2.23.1067 du 1er décembre 2023, relatif à l’application de la loi n° 58.23 portant régime de l’aide sociale directe. Ce projet prévoit une revalorisation du montant de l’aide forfaitaire, dont le seuil minimal passera de 500 à 600 dirhams à compter du 1er janvier 2027. D’autres augmentations seront programmées au cours des années suivantes, avec pour objectif d’atteindre 1.000 dirhams en 2031. items.title: JOJ Dakar 2026 : le Sénégal surclasse la France et se hisse au sixième rang mondial
items.description: Les Jeux olympiques de la jeunesse (JOJ) de Dakar 2026 sont decidement l'occasion pour le pays hote de briller aussi bien sur le plan de l'organisation que sur celui des performances sportives. a l'approche de la cloture, le Senegal occupe la sixieme place mondiale avec dix medailles, dont cinq en or et cinq en bronze. Il devance ainsi la France, septieme avec quatre medailles d'or, cinq d'argent et quatre de bronze. Le pays hote a engage 136 athletes dans les differentes disciplines de cette edition. a l'echelle continentale, le Senegal occupe la troisieme place, derriere l'ethiopie, qui totalise cinq medailles d'or et trois d'argent. L'egypte domine le classement africain et se hisse au quatrieme rang mondial avec six medailles d'or, une d'argent et cinq de bronze. Elle se place derriere la Russie, troisieme avec huit medailles d'or, quatre d'argent et deux de bronze, le Japon, deuxieme avec neuf titres, huit medailles d'argent et neuf de bronze, et la Chine, toujours en tete avec seize medailles d'or, huit d'argent et six de bronze. Les medailles les plus marquantes du Senegal La premiere medaille senegalaise de ces JOJ a ete remportee le 1er novembre par le judoka Matar Diop, medaille de bronze dans la categorie masculine des moins de 66 kg. La delegation s'est ensuite particulierement illustree en lutte de plage, decrochant trois titres olympiques grâce a elisabeth Diatta et Ndeye Khady Anna Diatta, sacrees respectivement dans les categories feminines des 55 kg et des 45 kg, ainsi qu'a Maguette Diop, vainqueur chez les hommes en 80 kg. Le Senegal a egalement remporte l'or en basket 3x3 masculin, le 9 novembre, tandis que la selection feminine a decroche le bronze. Le lendemain, Marie Sarr a ete sacree championne olympique de taekwondo dans la categorie des moins de 55 kg. Deux autres medailles de bronze ont ete obtenues dans cette discipline par Aïda Toure et Ameth Diop. Pour cette avant-derniere journee des JOJ, ce 12 novembre, plusieurs titres restent a attribuer, notamment en boxe, en taekwondo par equipes mixtes, en futsal, en escrime et en voile. Le programme comprend egalement les dernieres phases des competitions de beach handball et de breaking. Plusieurs athletes senegalais restent en lice, avec l'espoir d'enrichir encore le palmares du pays hote avant la ceremonie de cloture, prevue le 13 novembre.

items.title: Les Sénégalais en repêchage pour le bronze
items.description: Le Sénégal conserve une chance de monter sur le podium après sa défaite face à la Jordanie en quarts de finale ce jeudi matin . Les combattants sénégalais disputeront un match de repêchage face à l’Allemagne, prévu à 15h25, pour tenter de décrocher une place dans la course au bronze. Le relais sénégalais, composé d’Ibrahima Beye, Ameth Diop, Marie Sarr et Aïda Touré, s’est incliné face à la Jordanie sur le score de 2-0 en quarts de finale. Une défaite difficile après un début de rencontre encourageant. Battu lors du premier round sur le score de 60-43, le Sénégal espérait revenir dans la partie lors de la deuxième manche. Mais les Jordaniens ont renversé la situation en réalisant une remontée spectaculaire en moins d’une minute. Ils se sont finalement imposés 55-46, validant ainsi leur qualification pour les demi-finales. Le rêve de médaille reste toutefois intact. Dans le système de repêchage, les équipes éliminées en quarts de finale peuvent retrouver une chance de disputer une médaille de bronze, à condition que leur bourreau poursuive son parcours jusqu'aux demi-finales. C'est le cas du Sénégal, puisque la Jordanie a décroché son billet pour le dernier carré. Repêchés, les Sénégalais auront désormais une nouvelle occasion de se relancer face à l’Allemagne, battue en demi-finale par la Turquie. Le rendez-vous est fixé à 15h25. Une victoire leur permettrait de poursuivre leur parcours vers une éventuelle médaille de bronze. A.N

items.title: Who is Nvidia interim CEO Colette Kress?
items.description: Nvidia finance chief Colette Kress is set to take over as interim CEO from Jensen Huang, the company said on Thursday, putting her in charge of the chipmaker whose processors power the world’s most advanced supercomputers and AI data centres. The appointment comes after the board ousted co-founder and CEO Jensen Huang amid reports of two extramarital affairs, one with a woman alleged to be a Chinese spy . Here are five facts about Kress: CFO since 2013 Kress joined Nvidia in September 2013 as executive vice president and chief financial officer and has held the post since. She has appeared alongside Jensen Huang on the company’s quarterly earnings calls. Nvidia’s revenue was $4.13 billion in the fiscal year she joined and $215.9bn in fiscal 2026. Career before Nvidia Before Nvidia, Kress spent eight years in finance roles at Texas Instruments, then worked at Microsoft from 1997 to 2010. At Microsoft, she became chief financial officer of the Server and Tools division in 2006, with responsibility for its financial strategy, planning and reporting. She moved to Cisco in 2010 as senior vice president and chief financial officer of its Business Technology and Operations Finance organisation, where she was responsible for financial strategy and business development. She left for Nvidia in 2013. Education and experience Kress holds a bachelor of science degree in finance from the University of Arizona and a master of business administration degree from Southern Methodist University, according to Nvidia’s annual report filed with the US Securities and Exchange Commission. She joined Nvidia after nearly 25 years in finance roles at major technology companies, Fortune reported in 2024. She told Fortune Nvidia was the smallest company she had worked for when she started there in 2013. Contract terms Executive officers at Nvidia are employed at will and have no individual employment, severance or change-in-control agreements, according to the company’s proxy statement. Nvidia has said in earlier filings that many of its peer companies offer such agreements. Regulatory filings show Kress’ pay includes restricted stock units, including a March 2026 award that vests over four years. Wealth Forbes ranks Kress at 32 on its 2026 list of America’s richest self-made women. Her shares in the chip firm were valued at roughly $750 million, as of Wednesday’s close, down from more than $1bn at the stock’s peak last month.

items.title: Business
