items.title: Burkina Faso : 10 tonnes de ciment offertes à Faso Mêbo par la Mutuelle des travailleurs de la Boulangerie Wend Konta
items.description: La Mutuelle des travailleurs de la Boulangerie Wend Konta a effectué, ce 12 novembre 2026, un don de 10 tonnes de ciment et de 100 miches de pain au profit de l’initiative Faso Mêbo. À travers ce geste de solidarité, la structure entend apporter sa contribution aux efforts de développement et de construction du pays. La cérémonie de remise s’est déroulée sur le site de Faso Mêbo, en présence des représentants des deux structures. Prenant la parole à cette occasion, le superviseur de la Boulangerie Wend Konta, Moïse Tiendrébéogo, a expliqué les motivations de ce geste. Selon lui, cette contribution traduit l’engagement des travailleurs à accompagner les initiatives qui participent au développement national. « Le président du Faso a demandé à tous les fils du pays de s'y mettre pour la construction du pays. Nous, en tant que travailleurs du groupe Rimo Ajar, section boulangerie, avons décidé de faire une contribution, notre manière aussi de participer à la construction du pays », a-t-il déclaré. De son côté, le représentant du responsable de Faso Mêbo a salué cette initiative et exprimé sa reconnaissance à la Mutuelle des travailleurs de la Boulangerie Wend Konta pour cet acte de solidarité. La mutuelle compte plus de 5 000 travailleurs. À travers cette action, elle réaffirme son attachement aux valeurs de solidarité, de participation citoyenne et d’engagement collectif pour le développement du Burkina Faso. Grâce Kabré/ Bazié (Stagiaire) Faso7 L’article Burkina Faso : 10 tonnes de ciment offertes à Faso Mêbo par la Mutuelle des travailleurs de la Boulangerie Wend Konta est apparu en premier sur Faso7 .

items.title: Africa needs $4bn yearly to expand clean cooking access by 2030 – Samira Bawumia
items.description: Former Second Lady Hajia Samira Bawumia has called for an annual investment of about US$4 billion to accelerate Africa’s transition to clean cooking, warning that inadequate funding is worsening health risks, deforestation and gender inequalities. She said the continent’s continued reliance on firewood and other traditional cooking fuels was undermining public health, environmental sustainability and the economic empowerment of women and girls. Speaking as a panellist at the 31st United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31) in Antalya, Türkiye, Hajia Bawumia urged African governments, development partners and private-sector investors to make clean cooking a priority in the continent’s development and climate agenda. Citing estimates by the International Energy Agency (IEA), she said Africa required about US$4 billion annually to accelerate the adoption of cleaner cooking technologies by 2030. She warned that without sustained financing and stronger political commitment, millions of households would continue to depend on traditional cooking methods, with consequences for health, livelihoods and natural resources. Hajia Bawumia said women and girls were disproportionately affected by traditional cooking practices, spending considerable time collecting firewood, preparing meals and dealing with exposure to household smoke. She estimated that African women spend about 80 hours a week cooking, time she said could otherwise be devoted to education, economic activities and personal development. “The time it takes to collect firewood, to travel and to prepare meals takes a toll on girls and women. It affects their education,” she said. She argued that expanding access to clean cooking technologies should be treated not only as an environmental intervention but also as a means of advancing gender equality, improving livelihoods and reducing unpaid domestic work. “Anytime you talk about food systems, you have to talk about cooking. Anytime you talk about energy transition, you have to talk about clean cooking. Anytime you talk about women empowerment, you have to talk about clean cooking,” she stressed. The former Second Lady also warned that continued reliance on firewood was contributing to deforestation, with households depending on trees to meet their daily cooking needs. She expressed concern that economic trees were being felled for firewood in Ghana and other African countries, undermining efforts to protect natural forests. “This is a climate issue. In Ghana, for instance, and other African countries, most of the wood that is used for cooking is not sustainable. We are felling economic trees for firewood,” she said. She also identified emissions, including black carbon from traditional cooking methods, as an important climate concern requiring urgent attention. Hajia Bawumia acknowledged Ghana’s efforts to promote cleaner cooking, citing the adoption of national standards for clean cookstoves and the development of a National Clean Cooking Strategy and Investment Prospectus. She also referenced the distribution of three million improved cookstoves and initiatives to establish sustainable woodlots as interim measures to reduce pressure on natural forests while households transition to cleaner energy sources. One such initiative is the Woodlots for Households programme, implemented by the Council for Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR). She said the programme had reached about 1,000 households, with plans to expand its coverage. She further highlighted collaboration between the Energy Commission and the Ghana Education Service to integrate energy technologies and clean cooking solutions into the educational curriculum. According to her, exposing young people to alternative cooking technologies would help challenge traditional household practices and encourage the adoption of more sustainable methods. She also cited the establishment of two testing laboratories at the Columbia Institute of Science and Technology, her alma mater, to support research and testing of clean cooking technologies. Despite the interventions, Hajia Bawumia said Ghana needed stronger institutional coordination and sustained collaboration across sectors to make meaningful progress. She noted that clean cooking cuts across health, environment, education, energy and land management, making it difficult for a single institution to drive the agenda effectively. “The challenge is how to go about it and who owns it, because it is a multi-sectoral issue. You cannot leave it to just one sector,” she said. She urged governments, development organisations and private-sector investors to deepen partnerships, mobilise funding and expand public education to make cleaner cooking technologies affordable and accessible. She expressed optimism that sustained investment and coordinated action would accelerate Africa’s transition away from traditional cooking fuels, improving public health, supporting women’s economic empowerment and protecting natural resources. COP31 in Antalya, Türkiye, has brought together governments, international institutions, businesses and civil society organisations to advance global climate action and strengthen commitments to environmental sustainability.

items.title: UKGCC mobilises corporate, public support to strengthen neonatal care at PMLCH
items.description: The UK-Ghana Chamber of Commerce (UKGCC) has mobilised financial and material support for the Princess Marie Louise Children’s Hospital (PMLCH) in Accra to strengthen neonatal care and enhance security as its corporate responsibility initiative marking its 10th anniversary. The support comprised c ash donations totalling GHS923.165.00 which will fund the purchase of three specialised incubators for the hospital’s Neonatal Intensive Care Unit (NICU) amongst other things. The funds were raised through UKGCC’s public fundraising drive and contributions from member companies, including Fidelity Bank Ghana and Blue Skies Products Ghana LTD. Furthermore, UKGCC member company, G4S Security Services LTD. has installed a CCTV monitoring system across designated areas of the Hospital worth GHS67,917.44,in response to security and operational needs identified by the Hospital’s administration. Sustaining life at the NICU Speaking during the presentation ceremony to PMLCH, Adjoba Kyiamah, Executive Director of the UKGCC, shared the strategic vision behind the initiative, emphasising that marking a decade of trade facilitation and investment required leaving an indelible, life-saving imprint on the host community. “As the UKGCC celebrates ten years of driving economic growth and trade relations between the United Kingdom and Ghana, we recognise that true business sustainability is anchored in social well-being,” Kyiamah stated. “Equipping the NICU at Princess Marie Louise Children’s Hospital with state-of-the-art incubators enables us to put this to practice, while ensuring that fragile, premature infants are given the precise environmental conditions and real-time vital tracking they require to survive and thrive in advancement of the United Nations SDG 3.” The initiative also advances SDG 17, as Kyiamah extended her gratitude, on behalf of UKGCC’s Executive Council, UK-based Advisory Board and team to the corporate donors, UKGCC member company, IT Consortium’s digital crowdfunding Chango platform, and all the individuals who made donations, for their support. These contributions demonstrated the power of collective action. She also acknowledged the Ga Mantse Foundation whose own fundraising campaign for PMLCH is what first drew the UKGCC’s attention to the plight of the Hospital. Timely relief for paediatric care For her part, Dr. Mame Yaa Nyarko, Medical Superintendent of PMLCH, expressed appreciation to the UKGCC for placing the needs of children at the centre of its anniversary CSR initiative and also acknowledged the companies, foundation, and members of the public whose contributions made the intervention possible. “We are extremely grateful to the UK-Ghana Chamber of Commerce and to every company and individual who responded to the appeal. UKGCC’s support goes beyond facilitating the donations; it demonstrates the power of strategic partnerships, advocacy, and collaboration in addressing critical healthcare needs,” Dr. Nyarko noted. “For us at PMLCH, these funds represent an important contribution towards strengthening neonatal care and improving survival outcomes for newborns, particularly the most vulnerable infants who depend on specialised and timely medical attention. Especially as we celebrate Prematurity Awareness Month, this donation is timely and relevant for our sick and small babies. We also appreciate the installed and planned security enhancements which will contribute to a safer hospital environment. We believe that every child deserves a fighting chance at life, and partnerships such as this bring us closer to making that aspiration a reality.” Collective effort The campaign used documentary storytelling, interviews with hospital personnel and parents, social media advocacy, and donor engagement to raise awareness of the hospital’s neonatal equipment needs and mobilise support from businesses, foundations and members of the public. For UKGCC, the intervention reflects its commitment to extending the value of its business network beyond trade and investment to address important community needs. As UKGCC marks a decade of operations, Kyiamah said the initiative builds on previous fundraising efforts which supported the establishment of a clinical trials unit at the University of Ghana Medical Centre, and the Otumfuo Osei Tutu II Foundation. “Our previous fundraising efforts, alongside this latest initiative for PMLCH, demonstrate our belief that the relationships built through business can extend beyond commercial opportunities to make a meaningful contribution to society,” she said. The official presentation ceremony brought together representatives from UKGCC and senior Hospital administrators.

items.title: Le patron de Nvidia démissionne provoquant une onde de choc sur les marchés financiers
items.description: Le directeur général du groupe américain de technologie Nvidia, Jensen Huang, a démissionné jeudi de son poste provoquant une chute de 10% du titre du géant des semi-conducteurs dans les échanges avant l’ouverture de Wall Street, jeudi matin, et un onde de choc qui a affecté les marchés financiers à travers le monde. Le départ inattendu de Huang met fin à plus de trois décennies de direction de l’entreprise, dont il a été le co-fondateur, et a contribué également à en faire un acteur central de l’industrie technologique, puis de l’essor mondial de l’intelligence artificielle. L’action de Nvidia, qui s’échangeait mercredi à la clôture à 174,58 dollars, dégringolait jeudi matin à environ 158 dollars. Pour assurer la transition, le groupe a désigné sa directrice financière, Colette Kress, au poste de directrice générale par intérim, dans l’attente de la nomination d’un successeur permanent, croit savoir le Wall Street Journal. Aucun candidat évident ne semble se dégager, alors que Jensen Huang avait indiqué ne pas croire à une planification formelle de sa succession, relève le quotidien des milieux financiers. La crise a également pesé sur les marchés internationaux, les contrats à terme sur le Nasdaq, indice à forte composante technologique, reculant jeudi matin, alors que plusieurs indices asiatiques et des valeurs liées aux semi-conducteurs et à l’IA ont enregistré des baisses. Selon les analystes, le départ de Huang, intervenu sur fond de révélations concernant deux relations extraconjugales, soulève des interrogations sur la valorisation de Nvidia et sur la place centrale qu’occupe son dirigeant dans l’écosystème mondial de l’IA. La tourmente a déjà effacé plusieurs centaines de milliards de dollars de la capitalisation boursière du groupe. The post Le patron de Nvidia démissionne provoquant une onde de choc sur les marchés financiers appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: A possible Xi-Trump-Putin summit evokes 1945 Yalta carve-up of world
items.description: A possible China-US-Russia summit has prompted alarm of a modern-day Yalta Conference, with three powerful men carving up the world — with little regard for Ukraine, Europe and Taiwan or anyone else. But apart from an historic photo opportunity, the meeting between Presidents Xi Jinping, Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin at the Nov 18-19 APEC summit in Shenzhen will likely achieve little, analysts say. Spheres of influence When then US president Franklin D. Roosevelt, Britain’s Winston Churchill and Soviet leader Joseph Stalin met in Yalta in February 1945, they laid out the post-WWII settlement and new territorial boundaries in Europe. That meeting in Yalta, then in the Soviet Union and now in a part of Ukraine annexed by Russia in 2014, laid out the foundations for the Soviet domination of Eastern Europe and the Cold War. Ukraine’s President Volodymyr Zelensky has raised alarm that Shenzhen could be a Yalta-like “redistribution of spheres of influence” for the 21st century. At talks in Abu Dhabi this week — the first since February — Russian negotiators rattled Ukraine and its European supporters by pushing a review of the continent’s security architecture as part of any peace deal, with the US also floating a new framework. Russia’s delegation chief in Abu Dhabi, Vladimir Medinsky, fanned such fears by questioning the inclusion of Europe in further talks. The trilateral rankles because it signals “the idea that a few great powers can decide the security and future of other countries over their heads”, according to Tsiporah Fried at the Hudson Institute. The format alone “would already send a message about who counts, and whose interests can be negotiated by others”, she told AFP . Divergent interests Beyond the symbolism, however, divergent interests make the creation of a new world order in Shenzhen unlikely. Even the agenda reportedly remains contentious: Russia has suggested the meeting focus on Ukraine, Trump has pushed for talks on nuclear weapons and the Iran war, and China has remained tight-lipped on both. “The three parties have vastly different demands, making the management of expectations difficult. There is a high probability that talks could end without a breakthrough,” according to Wang Wen, dean of the Chongyang Institute for Financial Studies at Renmin University in Beijing. There are also few issues where input from all three leaders could bring progress. The main points of contention between Beijing and Washington are trade and the AI technology race, for instance. Beijing — which presents itself as a champion of multilateralism — has repeatedly said that Europe should be part of peace negotiations over Ukraine. German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier said that in a recent meeting, Xi showed “irritation” when the idea of the trilateral talks covering Ukraine came up. “He explicitly pointed out that this is a European conflict, in which the Europeans must also be at the table,” Steinmeier told ARD . On nuclear disarmament, China has long insisted that the US and Russia reduce their own giant nuclear arsenals before it agrees to talks on its own stockpile. The summit therefore is more likely to produce minor outcomes such as crisis hotlines or some cooperation on counter-terrorism, public health, or climate change, Wang told AFP . “There is no single enemy to unite all three great powers the way that the fight against Nazi Germany united Roosevelt, Churchill, and Stalin,” said Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at Australian National University. “It follows that piecemeal horse-trading is in; a grand bargain is out.” However, Taiwan — which China claims — will still be watching the meeting closely, Sung said. “If the Trump administration is open to abandoning one partner (Ukraine) out of convenience, then it can abandon another,” he said. A post-Shenzhen world The Trump administration has sought to reassert US dominance over the “Western hemisphere” — including by capturing Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro in January — but splitting the world among great powers like it’s 1945 may not guarantee security. China has opposed the logic of Yalta — the clandestine division of spheres of influence and major powers determining the fate of other nations — “from the very beginning”, according to Renmin University’s Wang. China could allay fears of a second Yalta by using the summit to “emphasise the defence of sovereignty and support for multilateral organisations”, Wang said. If Beijing uses the meeting to insist on European inclusion in talks regarding the continent’s security, it “could, in fact, open a new window for communication between China and Europe”, he said. “The original Yalta opened the path to the Korean War and Indochina Wars in addition to various conflicts and insurgencies across Asia, Africa, and Latin America,” said Chong Ja Ian at the National University of Singapore. Any Yalta 2.0 agreement “will almost certainly run into the same kinds of issues”, Chong said.

items.title: A $5.7 Trillion Face-Plant
items.description: Updated at 9:05 a.m. ET on November 12, 2026 Most of the major executives in the AI boom have weathered vicious attacks and major controversies in recent years, but one has stood out as bulletproof: Jensen Huang, the CEO of the global microprocessor giant Nvidia. That changed yesterday when, following revelations that Huang had at least two extramarital affairs, reports emerged that the company’s board was meeting to decide whether to remove him. Then, this morning, Huang resigned. Up until that moment, Nvidia, and by extension Huang, had felt like a stabilizing force in AI. Even if Anthropic and OpenAI faltered, Nvidia raked in profits: By some estimates, it has provided 90 percent of the advanced chips used in the AI industry. Elon Musk and Sam Altman may seem erratic or disingenuous, but Huang came off as steadfast and discerning. Dario Amodei’s messianism has led to tussles with the White House, but Huang and Donald Trump were chummy. Just last month, Nvidia’s valuation hit a sky-high $5.7 trillion—rivaled only by its own previous peak, from May. Huang was the AI boom’s king, and his kingdom was wealthy and, above all, secure. [ Read: Jensen Huang is too big to fail ] Then came news of Huang’s infidelity—including a liaison with an alleged Chinese spy—which ultimately led to Huang’s ouster. What happens next is uncertain: While Colette Kress, Nvidia’s chief financial officer, will serve as the interim CEO, Huang has run the company since 1993, when he co-founded the firm, and he has no clear successor. Nvidia’s stock has tumbled on the news, and the future of the company is in question. Silicon Valley, and perhaps the global economy, may be in jeopardy as well. It’s worth underscoring just how entrenched Nvidia is in the broader AI ecosystem. In addition to delivering the best chips in the business—there’s no ChatGPT or Claude without them—the company’s huge profits fuel an industry flywheel: The firm has guaranteed tens of billions of dollars to fledgling AI firms and data centers that, in turn, buy or rent Nvidia chips. These investments fuel the U.S. economy as a whole. One analysis found that just eight AI companies account for half of the gains in the S&P 500 since the launch of ChatGPT, in 2022. As much as a third of U.S. GDP growth this year is being driven by AI-related investments. None of that would have been possible without Nvidia. Within Silicon Valley, Huang has been heralded as almost clairvoyant. In its first decade, Nvidia was dedicated solely to making microprocessors for gaming consoles—a still-nascent but growing sector. Then, in 2006, the company debuted a way to adapt its chips for machine learning. Instead of being celebrated, Huang was derided . Nvidia’s stock crashed within a couple of years, and muddled along as the AI industry began to take shape. Nvidia’s impressive rise reinvented Huang’s identity within Silicon Valley as an era-defining leader. His company seemed to run like a well-oiled machine. “You want to refine the character of your company,” Huang said at a Stanford summit in 2024, and “greatness comes from character.” His strongest character trait seemed to be his unshakable confidence: “You’re not talking to somebody who woke up a loser. That loser attitude, that loser premise makes no sense to me,” he rebutted earlier this year, when asked about the threat of Chinese chipmakers catching up to Nvidia. When Silicon Valley seemed to lose its wits over AI models running rampant this past summer, Huang appeared nonplussed and offered to “send engineers in” to fix the problem. Lori Huang, his wife of 40-plus years, was also part of his narrative: “To build a company, you need somebody strong and you need somebody amazing like my wife,” Jensen said on a podcast earlier this year. “And she took care of everything.” She even helped introduce him to his trademark leather jacket. This was a man who purported to be so busy and single-mindedly focused on his company that he bragged about not knowing his phone number or home address. Despite a packed schedule, it appears he had enough time to have at least two affairs. On Sunday, he admitted to being romantically involved with Alice Huang, a Chinese businesswoman who, until recently, headed up Megaspeed, a Singaporean data-center company. Megaspeed has bought billions of dollars’ worth of Nvidia chips and is suspected of smuggling Nvidia technology to China, contravening U.S. export controls. She is also reportedly suspected by U.S. intelligence agents of being a spy. (China has denied this.) Up until Jensen Huang’s mea culpa, Nvidia had denied anything unethical or untoward in the CEO’s relationship with Alice Huang; a spokesperson insisted that “Jensen’s interactions with Ms. Huang are not unusual or unexpected.” Not unusual, indeed. The second affair, with Nvidia’s vice president of health care, was reported in The New York Times last night. Is the most powerful AI executive in the world hiding other secrets? Apparently Nvidia’s board of directors didn’t want to risk finding out. (Nvidia did not immediately respond to a request for comment.) In retrospect, all of the signs of slippery business practices and personal hubris were there. By the middle of 2025, Singapore-based customers—by then under considerable scrutiny as possible middlemen for China—accounted for one-fifth of Nvidia’s revenues. After news broke that the U.S. government had launched an investigation into Megaspeed for smuggling chips to China, Nvidia appeared to change to an accounting methodology that did not show any revenue from Singaporean customers. The Times has reported that Nvidia’s top lawyer tried to intervene in the investigation, which started in 2024. (Nvidia told the Times that the company works with the government to stop smuggling.) All the while, Huang has been lobbying heavily to lift export controls to China. This spring, Secretary of State Marco Rubio reportedly warned Trump about Huang’s affair with an alleged Chinese spy while the two were on an Air Force One flight en route to Beijing. Trump apparently did not take action on the matter. This week, the president said that he thinks Huang is “a very honorable guy, and I feel very confident that he’ll be in good shape.” Following the recent allegations, the tech industry closed ranks around its king, arguing that Huang had made a mistake but was too valuable to really hold to account. Musk and a cadre of venture capitalists (along with Trump) all said that, essentially, Huang was “too big to fail,” as my colleague Charlie Warzel wrote . Perhaps Nvidia is still too big to fail, but Huang isn’t. His departure proves that the laws of physics still apply, no matter how wealthy or powerful you may be: There are consequences to reckless behavior. You can claim greatness one day, and still wake up a loser the next. In the end, Huang and the Nvidia board were still heeding the former CEO’s own advice, dispensed in a talk in 2003: “Corporate culture in our case is about intellectual honesty. Intellectual honesty to us means that we have the ability to be self-critical, that we have the ability to recognize we’ve made mistakes.”

items.title: Elections du 07 février 2027 : le Rdpc veut renforcer le nombre de femmes et de jeunes parmi ses candidats
items.description: © DR Le Comité central du Rassemblement démocratique du peuple camerounais (Rdpc) a rendu publiques les modalités et la procédure d’investiture des candidats au double scrutin municipal et législatif. Le Rassemblement démocratique du peuple camerounais (Rdpc) entre dans la phase des investitures et sélection des candidats qu’il va présenter au double scrutin législatif et municipal du 07 février prochain. Le Comité central du parti a rendu publique le 11 novembre 2026 la circulaire précisant les modalités et la procédure des investitures et sélection des candidats. L’une des consignes qui apparait à la lecture du document est relative à l’équilibre des genres et des générations. A ce sujet, la circulaire signée du secrétaire général du Comité central, le vice-Premier ministre Jean Nkuete, insiste sur le « renforcement substantiel des femmes, des jeunes et de nouvelles figures tant parmi les candidats titulaires et les candidats suppléants ». Critère d’investiture des listes de candidatures, le renforcement des effectifs des femmes et des jeunes en particulier s’inscrit dans la mise en œuvre des engagements du 8è mandat du président de la République, président national du parti. Ce critère marque le prolongement de l’annonce du Comité central dans sa circulaire relative à la célébration du 44è anniversaire d’accession à la magistrature suprême du président Paul Biya couplé au 1 er anniversaire de la prestation de serment. En perspective des élections, le parti demandait aux femmes et aux jeunes en octobre dernier de se préparer de manière active et efficace. Il les encourageait à conquérir davantage les postes lors du prochain scrutin. Derrière la mesure se trouve la volonté de la hiérarchie du parti de donner plus de chances aux jeunes, aux femmes, aux minorités d’intégrer les sphères de décision et de mise en œuvre de la politique du chef de l’Etat au niveau local. La consigne figure parmi les critères de liste retenus par l’instance du parti pour l’investiture des candidats. Les listes de candidats doivent prendre en compte les composantes ethniques locales et du cosmopolitisme. Elles doivent inclure les minorités et les militants en situation de handicap. Elles doivent éviter la non-concentration des responsabilités politiques et des postes électifs par une même famille, un même groupe ethnique, un même clan, un même village, une même commune… Ces critères de liste s’associent aux critères individuels. Ils sont relatifs au militantisme reconnu et établi dans la circonscription, la popularité et l’influence positive, la probité morale exemplaire ou encore la capacité à saisir la complexité sociopolitique et socioéconomique de l’environnement. Ils s’imposent aussi aux jeunes et aux femmes, rendant ainsi difficile la capacité de certains jeunes à pouvoir s’imposer. Néanmoins, le parti a prévu la commission centrale de supervision des investitures, la commission régionale de supervision, de suivi et de contrôle ainsi que la commission départementale de sélection pour veiller à l’application de ces critères et opérer des arbitrages nécessaires. Cet article Elections du 07 février 2027 : le Rdpc veut renforcer le nombre de femmes et de jeunes parmi ses candidats est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

items.title: GHIB partners with property specialists to connect African clients with London residential developments
items.description: Ghana International Bank plc (GHIB) has announced a collaboration with Daniel Ford International and the Berkeley Group to provide African clients with information on selected residential developments in London, alongside access to the bank’s UK banking services. The initiative was unveiled at an event in Accra, targeting high-net-worth individuals, entrepreneurs, business owners and senior executives across the continent who have international banking needs. Through the collaboration, prospective property buyers can access information on selected residential developments within the Berkeley Group’s portfolio, with property advisory services provided by Daniel Ford International. GHIB said its role would be limited to providing banking services to eligible customers and would not extend to recommending, advising on, arranging or endorsing any particular property purchase. The initiative comes as Africa’s affluent population continues to attract attention from international financial institutions and property businesses. The Africa Wealth Report 2026, published by New World Wealth, estimates that the continent has just over 127,000 US-dollar millionaires, defined in the report as individuals with at least US$1 million in liquid wealth. Nigeria accounts for an estimated 8,100 millionaires, while Ghana has approximately 2,600, according to the report. GHIB says the collaboration forms part of its efforts to expand its personal banking services to affluent customers across its African markets, particularly those seeking UK-based banking solutions. Established in London in 1959, GHIB has operated for more than six decades, supporting trade, investment and corporate banking relationships between Africa and international markets. The bank is now seeking to broaden its personal banking proposition through services for affluent African clients with cross-border financial requirements. Commenting on the collaboration, GHIB Chief Banking Officer, Ophelia Attobrah, said the initiative responds to the growing international banking needs of African professionals and business leaders. “At GHIB, we understand that many successful African professionals, entrepreneurs and business leaders increasingly have international banking needs, including when considering residential property ownership in the United Kingdom. Our proposition is designed to provide banking services that can support customers with their UK banking requirements, should the customer elect to pursue them,” she said. She said the bank’s Premier and Classic Accounts were UK-based services intended to help customers manage their international banking requirements, including those that may arise in connection with property acquisitions. “Our role is limited to providing appropriate banking services to eligible customers. Decisions concerning whether to acquire property, and which property to acquire, remain entirely with the customer,” she added. Mrs Attobrah said although the initiative was launched in Ghana, it was intended to serve existing and prospective customers across the bank’s African footprint. “This proposition is open to both existing and prospective GHIB customers in all the African markets we serve. We see significant opportunity to support affluent clients across West Africa and beyond as their international banking needs evolve, helping them manage cross-border financial requirements while maintaining strong connections to the continent,” she said. GHIB said access to its accounts would remain subject to its eligibility requirements, onboarding procedures, customer due diligence and applicable terms and conditions. The bank also clarified that it does not provide property, investment, mortgage, tax or legal advice through the collaboration. Customers interested in any of the developments are expected to make their own assessments and seek independent professional advice where necessary.

items.title: Canadian mining company signs MoU with Mari Energies in South Asia push
items.description: Ivanhoe Mines signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) with Mari Energies on Thursday, the Canadian company’s chairman Robert Friedland said on the sidelines of the Pakistan Minerals Investment Forum. Friedland said Ivanhoe is in the early stages of setting up a local office in Pakistan and will sign another MoU on Friday. Mari Energies’ mining unit, Mari Minerals, has multiple mineral exploration projects, including copper and gold in Pakistan. The partnership marks the Canadian miner’s entry into South Asia, expanding its presence beyond its major mineral projects in southern Africa. “We’re excited to be here in Pakistan,” Friedland said. ‘Significant evidence’ of placer gold in Punjab rivers, says CM Maryam At the forum, Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz said that there was “significant evidence” of “sufficient quantities” of placer gold flowing in the province’s five rivers. Maryam said Punjab was the land of five rivers and that gold was “literally flowing” in all five, particularly in the areas of Mianwali and Attock. Describing Pakistan as a “pot of gold”, she said its wealth lay both above and beneath the ground and needed to be explored and converted into tangible wealth. “The wealth beneath Punjab was never a problem, never a problem, just like the whole of Pakistan, just like all four provinces and the federating units. The chaos above ground was the actual problem,” she said. Maryam said the provincial mines and minerals department’s revenue stood at around Rs10 billion two and a half years ago but had since increased to Rs40bn. “And it is just the beginning,” she added. She also highlighted the province’s iron ore reserves, saying Chiniot had 261.5 million tonnes of iron ore. She said the provincial government was taking steps to facilitate investment in the mining sector and create an enabling environment for investors. The Punjab chief minister said her role as chief executive of the country’s most populous province was to facilitate investors and create an enabling environment by eliminating red tape, bureaucratic delays and unnecessary hurdles. The provincial government was offering one-window facilitation to ensure investors did not have to run from pillar to post to complete the necessary procedures, she added. Maryam said the government was also making substantial capital investments to reduce investors’ capital expenditure and prevent them from having to tie up funds in purchasing expensive land. Additionally, the government was offering concessional financing of up to Rs5 billion and would provide solar-powered energy solutions to investors to help offset high energy and fuel costs. Dar says provincial partnership vital for mineral development Dar said Pakistan’s constitutional framework made provincial partnership indispensable, adding that the provinces were essential partners in the national undertaking and that their constitutional authority and ownership of mineral resources must be respected. Addressing the event, he said the federal government was working alongside provincial governments and their leadership through national coordination, investment facilitation, policy alignment and international engagement. Dar said Pakistan’s mineral resources were central to the next phase of the country’s economic transformation, stressing the need to diversify exports, strengthen the industrial base and attract long-term investment. He said Pakistan possessed substantial and diverse mineral resources, including significant copper and gold potential along the Tethyan metallogenic belt in the west of the country. The country also had deposits of iron ore, chromite, lead, zinc, coal, rock salt, marble, gypsum, gemstones and other industrial minerals. The deputy PM said the Reko Diq copper-gold project in Balochistan demonstrated the potential of international expertise, national participation and provincial ownership in attracting major long-term investment. He stressed that Pakistan’s ambition should extend beyond extracting minerals and exporting them in raw form, saying the country needed to develop the capacity to process and refine them, as well as manufacture mineral-based products domestically. Dar said Balochistan was central to Pakistan’s mineral future, adding that the development of its resources should contribute meaningfully to the provincial economy and the well-being of its people. He also emphasised the importance of local employment, skills development and the participation of Pakistani companies, saying local communities must be active participants in and beneficiaries of mineral development. The deputy prime minister further stated that environmental protection, workers’ safety and the rehabilitation of mining sites were essential to a successful minerals industry. The Reko Diq copper-gold project in Balochistan is one of Pakistan’s most ambitious mining ventures, with significant potential to boost the country’s mineral wealth through the extraction of gold and copper. Designed as an open-pit mining and processing operation , the project will initially process 45 million tonnes of ore annually, with capacity expected to double to 90m tonnes after the completion of Phase 2. The mine has an estimated operational life of 37 years, which could potentially extend to 80 years through further exploration and resource development.

items.title: The CEO, the Spy, and a Crisis for AI
items.description: Subscribe here: Apple Podcasts | Spotify | YouTube | Overcast | Pocket Casts Reports of a second compromising affair may be the undoing of the Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, even though the first affair was with an alleged Chinese spy. Earlier this week, tech titans were going out of their way to minimize the scandal at Nvidia. Huang had confessed to an affair with an alleged foreign agent, but he was “irreplaceable,” according to Elon Musk. Huang had potentially put trade secrets and national security at risk, but he was an “honorable guy,” said President Trump, and “he probably has an excuse for it.” The billionaire hedge-fund manager Bill Ackman posted on X, “Onward,” implying: Move along—nothing to see here. Huang, it seemed, was too big to fail. Interested parties were more willing to ignore the obvious dangers than contemplate what it might mean to lose the man so singularly identified with the company at the center of the AI boom, the company so important that it might be currently propping up the U.S. economy. That was true until Wednesday, when news broke of a second affair Huang had, with an executive at Nvidia who reports directly to him. Nvidia’s board met to consider Huang’s future, a move that Atlantic staff writer Charlie Warzel describes as “taking a Jenga block out” of the AI tower. Now Huang has resigned. Staff writers Shane Harris, who covers intelligence agencies, and Warzel, who covers the tech industry, discuss on Radio Atlantic both the espionage and the business. Harris considers how China might have pulled this off, and what secrets they might have obtained. Warzel considers what the future of Nvidia, and the AI boom more broadly, might look like without its leader. This episode of Radio Atlantic taped before Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s resignation. A transcript of the episode is forthcoming

items.title: Affaire Ndiaga Seck et Cie : le procès renvoyé au 14 décembre prochain
items.description: Le procès de l’affaire dite « Ndiaga Seck et Cie », impliquant 32 prévenus poursuivis pour plusieurs chefs d’accusation, a été renvoyé au 14 décembre prochain par le tribunal de grande instance de Louga, à l’issue de l’audience ouverte jeudi. Les prévenus ont fait leur apparition dans la salle d’audience correctionnelle aux environs de 9 h 44, sous le regard du public venu assister au procès. Après l’installation du juge et de ses collaborateurs, les prévenus ont été appelés à comparaître individuellement. Toutefois, l’absence de l’un des co-prévenus pour des raisons médicales, ainsi que l’indisponibilité de certains avocats de la défense, ont empêché la tenue des débats. Les conseils de la défense ont également indiqué ne pas avoir accès au dossier et sollicité la tenue du procès à huis clos. Au regard de ces différentes contraintes, le juge a décidé de renvoyer l’affaire au 14 décembre prochain. L’affaire remonte à avril 2026. Les 32 prévenus sont poursuivis pour association de malfaiteurs, actes contre nature, transmission volontaire du VIH/Sida, mise en danger de la vie d’autrui, collecte illicite de données à caractère personnel et harcèlement sexuel. Falel Pam

items.title: Kpélé: La COOPEC Enyo d’Adeta devient désormais une Société coopérative avec conseil d’administration
items.description: Adéta, 12 nov. (ATOP) – La Coopérative d’épargne et de crédit (COOPEC) Enyo d’Adéta a été transformée en Société coopérative (SCOOP) avec un conseil d’administration à l’issue d’une assemblée générale extraordinaire, le mercredi 11 novembre à Adéta. Cette transformation institutionnelle s’inscrit dans le cadre de l’adoption de la loi du 24 mars 2026 portant réglementation de la microfinance en République togolaise. Elle vise à mettre les textes fondamentaux en conformité avec les nouvelles dispositions légales tout en préservant l’essence même du modèle coopératif fondé sur la solidarité, la responsabilité, la proximité et la participation démocratique. Elle constitue également une opportunité stratégique pour consolider les acquis, renforcer la confiance des membres, préparer durablement l’avenir ainsi que pour répondre aux attentes des membres dans un environnement en constante mutation. L’assemblée a, au cours des travaux, examiné et adopté des documents structurants pour la vie de l’institution notamment les statuts de la Société coopérative avec conseil d’administration, le règlement intérieur, la convention d’affiliation avec la FUCEC-Togo, et le règlement financier du réseau. Ces textes juridiques ne constituent pas de simples instruments administratifs mais aussi définissent le cadre de gouvernance, les responsabilités des organes dirigeants, les règles de gestion et les relations qui unissent la société au réseau FUCEC- Togo. Leur adoption permet de renforcer la transparence, d’améliorer l’efficacité du pilotage institutionnel et de consolider les mécanismes de contrôle indispensables à une gestion saine et pérenne. Les travaux ont aussi permis d’élire les membres du conseil d’administration avec à leur tête M. Komi Agbeko pour un mandat de trois ans renouvelable une fois. Le secrétaire général de la préfecture de Kpélé, Arimou Saboutou a invité les responsables et les membres à privilégier le dialogue constructif, la cohésion et la recherche permanente du consensus afin que les résolutions issues des travaux bénéficient d’une adhésion collective. Le représentant du directeur général de la FUCEC-Togo, M. Adokou Ayawlovi a remercié les autorités pour l’intérêt constant qu’ils portent au développement du secteur de la microfinance. ATOP/SKD/BA

items.title: États-Unis : L’avocat de Modou Ngom confirme le dépôt d’un appel contre sa condamnation
items.description: L’avocat Christopher Bazeley confirme avoir été désigné pour défendre Modou Fall Ngom en appel de sa condamnation à 22 ans et six mois de prison dans l’Ohio. Si le dépôt de l’avis d’appel est désormais confirmé, les arguments de la défense restent à définir. L’avocat entend d’abord prendre connaissance du dossier et examiner les transcriptions du procès, dont la préparation devrait nécessiter quatre à six semaines. Modou Fall Ngom a interjeté appel de sa condamnation à 22 ans et six mois de prison aux États-Unis. Incarcéré dans l’État de l’Ohio, le Sénégalais conteste ainsi la décision judiciaire prononcée à son encontre. Contacté via Gmail, Christopher Bazeley, l’avocat chargé de sa défense en appel, a indiqué qu’un avis d’appel avait bien été déposé. « Je peux confirmer que je représente M. Ngom et que l’avis d’appel a été déposé », a-t-il précisé. Pour l’heure, l’avocat estime qu’il est prématuré de se prononcer sur les chances de succès de cette démarche. Il devra d’abord prendre connaissance de l’ensemble des pièces du dossier et effectuer les recherches juridiques nécessaires avant de définir précisément sa stratégie. L’examen du dossier dépend notamment de la préparation des transcriptions des audiences. Selon Christopher Bazeley, leur établissement devrait prendre environ quatre à six semaines. Ces documents permettront à la défense de disposer d’une retranscription détaillée des débats et des éléments de procédure nécessaires à l’analyse du jugement. En attendant l’analyse complète du dossier par son avocat, Modou Fall Ngom demeure sous le coup de sa condamnation à 22 ans et six mois de prison. La procédure d’appel est engagée, mais son issue reste incertaine. Yaya SOW

items.title: Burkina | Insémination artificielle : Près de 650 vaches déjà inséminées dans la région de Oubri
items.description: Dans le cadre de la modernisation de l’élevage et de l’amélioration de la productivité animale, le Ministère en charge de l’Agriculture poursuit le suivi de la campagne 2026-2027 de vaccination, de déparasitage, d’insémination artificielle et d’identification des animaux. Ce mercredi 11 novembre 2026, une délégation ministérielle, conduite par le ministre delegué, Amadou Dicko, s’est rendue dans la région de Oubri, où, deux sites d’élevage ont été visités, notamment à Bangrinzaaga, dans la commune de Mogteodo, et à Songnaba, dans la commune de Sourgoubila. Le premier site visité était celui de la commune de Mogtéodo dans le village de Bangrinzaaga. Sur ce site, les responsables ont pu constater l'effectivité des vaccins, des déparasitages des animaux ainsi que des insémininations. Il en est de même au niveau du deuxième site à Sourgoubila dans le village de Songnaba. Le MD vaccine un petit ruminant En effet, cette sortie a permis aux responsables d'apprécier de visu, le niveau d’exécution des activités, mais également échanger avec les producteurs sur les résultats obtenus et les difficultés rencontrées. À l’issue de la visite, le Directeur général du Centre de promotion de l'aviculture et de multiplication des animaux performants (CPAMAP), Ardiouma Sirima a fait état d’une mobilisation encourageante des éleveurs autour de la campagne 2026-2027 de déparasitage, de vaccination contre les maladies animales prioritaires et les zoonoses, ainsi que d’insémination artificielle. « Depuis le lancement de la campagne en septembre dernier, les activités ont effectivement démarré dans la région et les équipes ont déjà inséminé près de 650 vaches. Aussi la vaccination se poursuit et suit son cours », a-t-il indiqué. L'introduction de la boucle RIFD, pour faciliter l'identification du mouton Pour cette campagne, la région de Oubri ambitionne d’inséminer 5 000 vaches, avec un taux de réussite attendu d’au moins 50 %. Selon Ardiouma Sirima, les moyens techniques et les formations nécessaires ont été mobilisés pour atteindre cet objectif. Il a toutefois relevé certaines réticences chez des producteurs, qu’il a invités à s’approprier davantage cette technologie, présentée comme une opportunité d’amélioration de la productivité de leurs élevages. Le DG CPAMAP a également tenu à rassurer les éleveurs sur les interrogations d'ordre religieux, précisant qu'aucune prescription religieuse n'interdit cette pratique. En parallèle de l’insémination artificielle, la campagne met l’accent sur l’identification numérique des animaux à travers des boucles RFID. Ce dispositif permet d’attribuer un identifiant unique à chaque animal et de faciliter son suivi tout au long de sa vie. « Cela permet de lutter contre le vol du bétail, de retracer l’origine de l’animal, de connaître son historique sanitaire et de suivre sa filiation », a expliqué DG CPAMAP. Couplées à l’insémination artificielle, ces opérations constituent, selon lui, des leviers importants pour l’amélioration génétique, la sécurisation des productions animales et la modernisation de l’élevage. Issa Compaoré, salue l'accompagnement des autorités, avec la subvention des vaccins des bovins et la gratuité de celui des petits ruminant Du côté des producteurs, les actions engagées suscitent également de la satisfaction. Éleveur dans la commune de Mogtéodo, Issa Compaoré a salué l’accompagnement des agents sur le terrain, notamment en matière de soins vétérinaires et de conseils techniques. Il s’est particulièrement réjoui de la gratuité des vaccins destinés aux petits ruminants et de la subvention accordée à ceux des bovins. Concernant l’insémination artificielle, il a estimé que la réduction du coût constitue un véritable soulagement pour les éleveurs. « Au départ, le prix de l’insémination était fixé à 75 000 FCFA. Présentement, nous ne payons que 5 000 FCFA pour en bénéficier », a-t-il souligné. Ayant déjà fait inséminer cinq de ses vaches, dont deux ont mis bas et trois sont en gestation, il a affirmé constater les avantages de cette technique. À titre d’exemple, il a confié qu’un veau d’environ huit mois issu de cette pratique a suscité une offre de plus d’un million de FCFA. Malgré ces avancées, le producteur a évoqué des difficultés liées notamment à l’accès au parc de vaccination et à la disponibilité de l’eau. Il a ainsi sollicité l’accompagnement des autorités pour la réalisation d’un nouveau parc de vaccination et d’un forage afin d’améliorer les conditions de travail des éleveurs. Ardiouma Sirima, satisfait de la mobilisation des acteurs au cours de la campagne 2026-2027 Il faut noter que la visite terrain sur le suivi de la campagne 2026-2027 de vaccination, de déparasitage, d’insémination artificielle et d’identification des animaux a débuté le mardi 10 novembre 2026, dans le Nazinon et se poursuit le jeudi 12 novembre 2026 dans la région du Yaadga. Nadège KINDA Minute.bf

items.title: NAIMOS says personnel acted in self-defence during Manso Keniago clash that left six dead
items.description: The National Anti-Illegal Mining Operations Secretariat (NAIMOS) says the deaths recorded during Wednesday’s confrontation at Manso Keniago in the Ashanti Region resulted from an act of self-defence by its personnel. NAIMOS Spokesperson, Paa Kwesi Schandorf, said the personnel acted in self-defence during the confrontation with residents and suspected illegal miners. He disclosed this on JoyNews’ Upfront programme hosted by Blessed Sogah. “That (the deaths) happened because they confronted the NAIMOS task force. A mob descended on the task force. The task force initially fired warning shots to disperse them and de-escalate the situation, but they were determined, insisting on the NAIMOS, and what compelled the NAIMOS, under the circumstances, to, in the interest of self-defence, deter them, and that is how, unfortunately, they lost their lives,” he explained. Watch the his full comment below. The incident occurred on Wednesday afternoon when some residents and suspected illegal miners reportedly attempted to prevent NAIMOS personnel from tracking excavators seized from the area. Preliminary accounts indicate that the group blocked the road and pelted the personnel’s vehicles with stones, shattering the windscreens of some of them. The confrontation initially left three people dead, but the death toll has since risen to six. The incident has also triggered tension in the community, with angry youth reportedly besieging the palace of the paramount chief and attempting to attack the District Chief Executive (DCE), whom they accused of failing to contain the situation.

items.title: Lutte contre la criminalité urbaine : Un réseau de malfrats démantelé par la Police Nationale à Ouagadougou
items.description: Le Commissariat de Police de l’Arrondissement (CPA) n°09 de la ville de Ouagadougou, dans le cadre de la lutte contre l’insécurité en général et la criminalité urbaine en particulier, a mis fin aux activités illicites d’un réseau de malfrats spécialisés, entre autres, dans les actes de grand banditisme, agressions et vols à main armée, usurpation d’identité, recel, vente et consommation de stupéfiants. Il ressort du mode opératoire du gang que ses membres sillonnaient nuitamment en binôme les artères de la ville de Ouagadougou, notamment les quartiers Yagma, Marcoussis, Toudoubwéogo, Kamboinsin, ainsi que celles des communes environnantes de Ouagadougou telles que Pabré, Laye et Boussé, à la recherche de lieux de commerce vulnérables à leur action. Leurs cibles de prédilection étaient les stations-service, les boutiques de vente de marchandises et les boutiques de transactions électroniques. Dès qu’une cible était identifiée, à l’aide d’un pistolet automatique ou d’une Kalachnikov, ils tenaient en respect la victime et la dépouillaient de ses numéraires, téléphones et autres biens. Pour éviter de se faire repérer, ces malfrats portaient des cache-nez et n’hésitaient pas à ouvrir le feu sur leurs victimes dès lors que celles-ci manifestaient une quelconque résistance ou tentaient de crier à l’aide. Les biens ainsi volés étaient partagés entre eux et une partie était même réinvestie dans la vente de marchandises diverses. Le préjudice causé par le groupe est estimé à environ 10.000.000 FCFA. Grâce à la collaboration des populations, les enquêteurs ont, au moment de l’interpellation des membres actifs du groupe, saisi plusieurs objets dont trois (03) Kalachnikovs, deux (02) pistolets automatiques, des munitions, des motos et des marchandises diverses. La Police Nationale réitère ses remerciements à tous les citoyens grâce à qui ces résultats ont été atteints. Elle les exhorte à plus de vigilance et de prudence autour d’eux et à toujours poursuivre la dynamique de collaboration avec les forces de l’ordre via les numéros verts que sont le 17, le 16 et le 1010. La Police Nationale, une force publique au service des citoyens ! Minute.bf

items.title: Take a look at the new Ghana cedi notes introduced by the Bank of Ghana
items.description: The Bank of Ghana has introduced upgraded Ghana cedi banknotes with enhanced security features, improved durability, and more convenient, portable sizes. The notes will be in circulation from December 1, 2026. Dubbed the Ghana Heritage Series, the new notes are designed to strengthen cedi security, improve convenience in everyday transactions, and inspire renewed national pride in Ghana’s currency. The upgraded banknotes feature distinctive designs showcasing national heroes, historic sites, monuments and, for the first time, Adinkra symbols. Speaking at the launch, Bank of Ghana Governor Dr Johnson Pandit Asiama said a national currency goes beyond serving as a medium of exchange. He explained that it reflects a country’s ability to manage its monetary affairs through its own institutions and provides the foundation for economic activity. “This launch is more than the introduction of upgraded notes. It is an opportunity for us to reaffirm our responsibility to protect the cedi, to celebrate the heritage that defines us and prepare our currency for the demands of a changing world,” he stated. Dr Asiama said that a currency’s credibility depends on sound policies, effective institutions, and the confidence of the people who use it. Read Also: Learn about the 8 personalities, landmarks, and symbols featured on the new Heritage Cedi notes He added that the Ghana Heritage Series marks another step in the Bank’s ongoing efforts to modernise currency management while preserving public confidence in the country’s national currency.

items.title: El Congreso se divide sobre dos decretos de vivienda en la resaca de la huelga y el arranque de la campaña electoral
items.description: En plena resaca de la gran movilización del miércoles en las calles de España con la huelga general por la crisis de la vivienda y a unas horas del inicio oficial de la campaña electoral, la Diputación Permanente del Congreso ha convalidado un decreto que prohíbe los desahucios, prorroga los alquileres dos años y con un tope de subida del 2%, pero ha rechazado otro que pretendía extender la moratoria de esos contratos de manera automática e indefinida. Han comparecido dos ministros, por lo que formalmente se han celebrado dos debates, pero en realidad solo una discusión sobre cómo abordar la solución a ese problema transversal, que se ha resuelto en dos bloques políticos enfrentados. El Gobierno del PSOE, Sumar y sus aliados parlamentarios de izquierdas han votado los dos y han salvado solo el primero . La derecha representada por PP, Vox, UPN y Junts ha rechazado ambos y ha tumbado, con el PNV, el segundo, con medidas más ambiciosas que consideraron “hipócritas” o demasiado radicales. items.title: GIPA CEO challenges private sector to demand accountability from public institutions
items.description: The Chief Executive Officer of the Ghana Investment Promotion Authority (GIPA), Simon Madjie, has challenged private sector players to demand greater accountability and efficiency from public institutions, saying businesses must play an active role in improving Ghana’s business environment. According to him, businesses should not tolerate unnecessary bureaucratic delays, particularly when they have fulfilled all the requirements for services to be delivered within stipulated timelines. Mr. Madjie made the remarks at the 15th Ghana Economic Forum, organised by the Business and Financial Times (B&FT) in Accra, under the theme: “From Stabilisation to Scale: Mobilising Capital, Technology and Policy for Ghana’s Next Industrial Wave.” Mr. Madjie also urged companies to insist on timely service delivery and report public officials who failed to meet their obligations. “If I have five days to register you and your documents are right, you must demand that I register you within five days. And if I don’t do it, report it through the system and report it to the head,” he said. He stressed that the private sector was a critical stakeholder in public sector reforms and must actively hold public institutions accountable to ensure efficient service delivery and create a more business-friendly environment. Beyond institutional accountability, Mr. Madjie called for greater investor patience and access to long-term financing to support private sector growth, particularly in manufacturing and participation in global value chains. He noted that Ghana’s strong trading culture had created an appetite for quick returns, making it difficult for businesses that require substantial long-term investments to attract patient capital. “Manufacturing and global value chains take time, so people must be patient,” he said.

items.title: Government may turn to alternative bitumen suppliers if GoEnergy fails to deliver – Agbodza
items.description: The Minister of Roads and Highways, Governs Kwame Agbodza, has urged GoEnergy Company Limited (GOE), a wholly owned subsidiary of Goil Plc, to ensure a consistent and timely supply of bitumen to road contractors to help prevent shortages of the critical construction material from delaying projects. He said the government had deliberately directed a significant share of its bitumen procurement through GoEnergy to secure competitive prices and establish a reliable supply chain for road construction. He, however, cautioned that the arrangement must guarantee adequate and timely deliveries, warning that the government would seek alternative suppliers if GoEnergy failed to meet contractors’ requirements. “We decided that much of the bitumen product would come from GoEnergy, but if they are not able to supply the required quantities, we will have to take a different route and look for alternative suppliers,” he said. Leading a team of engineers to inspect reconstruction of the 53.35-kilometre Have–Hohoe road in the Volta Region on Tuesday (Nov 10), he said, “If you cannot provide the bitumen, we will look for alternative suppliers. We were trying to give a competitive advantage to GoEnergy, but if they cannot, we have no time to wait for anybody,” he said. The minister expressed these sentiments after he took a swipe at Greenhouse International Development (GH) Limited for the sluggish pace it was executing the Have-Hohoe road project. But the contractor raised concerns about delays in accessing bitumen, a key material required for asphalt production and the surfacing of roads. Speaking on behalf of the company, its Administrator, Gerome Chen, cited delays in the supply of bitumen as one of the challenges affecting the pace of work, with the material reportedly arriving on September 10. Such delayed supply had contributed to the delay in its operations, he said. He explained that the company used performance grade (PG) bitumen for its asphalt production and that the limited number of suppliers in Ghana had made it difficult to secure the material. “Sometimes, because our asphalt is PG, Ghana has only one company that can provide good bitumen. From September 10 to October 20 this year, Ghana did not have PG bitumen,” Mr Chen said. PG bitumen, also known as Performance Grade bitumen, is an asphalt binder classified according to its ability to withstand specified high and low pavement temperatures. Responding, Mr Agbodza said the government’s decision to rely significantly on GoEnergy was intended to leverage its supply capacity and obtain the material at competitive rates. He, however, said the arrangement must not become a source of delays in project execution. He indicated that contractors needed consistent access to bitumen to maintain their construction schedules and deliver projects within the agreed timelines. The minister pointed out that while the government was committed to securing competitive prices for construction materials, the availability of bitumen must not compromise the delivery of road infrastructure projects.

items.title: At COP31, PM Shehbaz calls for grant-based finance, resilience funding for climate-vulnerable countries
items.description: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Thursday called for grant-based finance and improved resilience and adaptation funds for climate-vulnerable countries at COP31, being held in Turkiye’s Antalya. This year’s summit focuses on transitioning toward a low-carbon future. Delegates from nearly 200 countries are meeting in the Mediterranean resort city of Antalya as global greenhouse gas emissions show little sign of falling, while wars, inflation and other crises compete for political attention. Addressing the summit, PM Shehbaz highlighted Pakistan’s efforts to promote clean energy but warned that “national effort cannot replace a fair and just global response”. “When climate disasters strike, vulnerable countries need timely help and finance that does not deepen their debt,” he said, adding that Pakistan called for “grant-based finance, including public-private partnerships, alongside a significant increase in resilience and adaptation funds, which amount to survival funds, especially for struggling economies”. He said clean energy sources accounted for nearly 55pc of Pakistan’s energy needs, adding that the country was advancing electric mobility and had set a target of reducing projected emissions by about 50pc by 2035. Recalling the 2025 floods in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa’s Buner district , the prime minister said: “In August 2025, a young man in Buner was just two days away from his wedding when flash floods swept through his village. A home preparing for celebrations became a house of mourning.” “Their grief was personal, yet the warning signs were global,” the prime minister said, noting that this was the story of “millions of people in Pakistan and across the developing world”. “People who have contributed the least to climate change bear its heaviest consequences,” he added. Addressing the summit, PM Shehbaz also recalled the 2022 floods in Pakistan, noting the economic damage and mass displacement the catastrophe caused. More than 1,700 people lost their lives, and economic losses exceeded $30bn, the prime minister said. PM Shehbaz recalled his speech at the UN General Assembly in 2022. “I had warned that what is happening in Pakistan will not stay in Pakistan, and unfortunately, that warning has become a stark reality. “The future we feared has become the present we are living,” he said. Underscoring the need for global solidarity, the premier remarked, “Climate change knows no borders and no nation can face it alone. Solidarity must mean real action.” He then expressed gratitude to Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan for his country’s support for Pakistan during the 2010 and 2022 floods. Addressing the summit, PM Shehbaz also warned against the weaponisation of water. “No nation should be allowed to put the lives and livelihoods of people downstream at risk. Water-sharing agreements must be honoured in letter and spirit,” the premier said. Concluding his address, PM Shehbaz said world leaders had gathered at the summit to “shoulder a shared responsibility to protect life on this earth”. “Let our success be measured not by promises we make here but by the families we protect, the resources we deliver, and the meaningful action we sustain,” he said. Later, upon his departure from Antalya, the premier expressed his “deep appreciation for the warmth and affection of my dear brother, President Recep Tayyip Erdogan”. He praised Erdogan’s “powerful” address, particularly his words regarding the situation in Gaza, which he called one of “the most poignant moments” of the summit. “His graciousness in hosting a luncheon meeting with me today, despite an exceptionally busy schedule […] is yet another reflection of his friendship and generosity,” he added. “Pakistan and Turkiye are bound by an enduring brotherhood. We will stand together, always.” Meetings on the sidelines of the summit Separately, PM Shehbaz held another series of meetings on the sidelines of the COP31 summit, including with the Turkish president. The Prime Minister’s Office (PMO), said that PM Shehbaz and Erdogan reaffirmed the deep-rooted, historic, and brotherly ties between Pakistan and Turkiye, and expressed satisfaction at the positive trajectory of bilateral relations. “The prime minister and the president held wide-ranging discussions on avenues to further enhance bilateral cooperation, with particular focus on trade and investment, defence collaboration, energy cooperation and connectivity,” it said. “Both leaders emphasised the importance of expediting the implementation of ongoing initiatives and exploring new opportunities to further deepen economic engagement. They also exchanged views on the evolving regional situation and broader global developments,” it said. It said that the premier highlighted the ongoing efforts by regional countries, particularly members of the Makkah Accord , to promote de-escalation and dialogue. It said that the Turkish president appreciated Pakistan’s constructive role and mediation efforts which led to the signing of the Islamabad memorandum of understanding (MoU) between Iran and the US. “The prime minister thanked President Erdogan for his steadfast support and close coordination throughout Pakistan’s entire diplomatic effort. Both leaders underscored the importance of adherence by all parties to their commitments under the Islamabad MoU to ensure durable and lasting peace in the wider region,” it said. “Both leaders reaffirmed their steadfast support for each other on issues of core national interest, reflecting the enduring tradition of mutual trust and solidarity between Pakistan and Turkiye. They also reaffirmed their resolve to further strengthen the strategic partnership between Pakistan and Turkiye, building on fraternal ties, and a shared vision for peace and prosperity,” it said. The prime minister also met the president of Sudan’s Transitional Sovereignty Council, General Abdel Fattah al-Burhan. A PMO statement said Shehbaz reaffirmed Pakistan’s longstanding ties with Sudan and reiterated Islamabad’s support for the country’s sovereignty, unity and territorial integrity. He also expressed solidarity with the Sudanese people amid the prevailing challenges. The two leaders had a productive exchange on ways to further strengthen bilateral relations in various areas of mutual interest, it added. They also exchanged views on the challenges posed by climate change and emphasised the importance of enhanced international cooperation to address its impact, particularly on developing countries. Both sides reaffirmed their commitment to maintaining close coordination at multilateral forums, it said. The premier also held a meeting with the president of Finland, Alexander Stubb. According to the PMO, the meeting provided an opportunity to review Pakistan–Finland relations and strengthen cooperation in areas of mutual interest. It said PM Shehbaz reaffirmed Pakistan’s desire to “translate the longstanding and friendly relations into a forward-looking partnership encompassing trade and investment, education and skills development, technology, climate resilience and people-to-people contacts”. He also noted the considerable potential to increase bilateral trade and welcomed the presence of Finnish companies in Pakistan, it added. The statement said PM Shehbaz also encouraged greater business-to-business engagement, technology transfer and investment in telecommunications, advanced manufacturing, clean technologies and mining. “The two leaders exchanged views on climate change, disaster risk reduction and environmental cooperation. The prime minister expressed interest in Finnish technical expertise in flood forecasting, water management, climate-resilient agriculture, glacier monitoring and early-warning systems,” the statement said. “Underlining the importance of dialogue, mediation and peaceful settlement, the two leaders exchanged views on ongoing diplomatic efforts for peaceful and durable solutions to the conflicts in Ukraine and West Asia,” it added. The statement further said that President Stubb appreciated Pakistan’s role in facilitating dialogue and mediation between the US and Iran. “The two leaders reaffirmed the importance of maintaining regular engagement and exploring practical avenues to deepen bilateral cooperation. The prime minister reiterated the invitation to President Stubb to undertake an official visit to Pakistan at a mutually convenient time,” it said. Further, the prime minister also met the president of Iraq, Nizar Mohammed Saeed Amidi. The PMO said PM Shehbaz congratulated President Amidi and the people of Iraq on the successful conduct of parliamentary elections and formation of the new government. “He reaffirmed Pakistan’s steadfast support for Iraq’s sovereignty, territorial integrity, national unity and stability,” it said. “The two leaders reaffirmed the longstanding brotherly relations between Pakistan and Iraq, rooted in shared faith, historical bonds and strong people-to-people contacts. Expressing satisfaction over the positive momentum in bilateral relations, they underscored the importance of sustained high-level exchanges and institutional engagement,” the statement said. The statement said that the premier also extended an invitation to President Amidi to visit Pakistan at a mutually convenient time. “The two sides reviewed the entire spectrum of bilateral cooperation, with particular focus on trade, investment, manpower, reconstruction, agriculture, and defence,” the statement said. “The prime minister appreciated Iraq’s facilitation for Pakistani zaireen (pilgrims). The two leaders also exchanged views on regional and international developments and reaffirmed their commitment for close coordination at multilateral fora,” it said. Pakistan stresses clean energy On Tuesday, PM Shehbaz addressed a high-level dialogue on clean energy transition, titled ‘ 35 by 35: Powering the Future ’, where he highlighted Pakistan’s solar power boom. “In just two years, Pakistan has added nearly 22 gigawatts of rooftop solar capacity — a quiet revolution by ordinary citizens seeking affordable power and a cleaner, more predictable future.” He had affirmed that Pakistan fully supports the ‘ 35-by-35 Global Electrification Pledge ’, wherein countries agree to aim to increase electricity’s share of total final energy consumption to around 35 per cent by 2035 in line with global climate objectives. The prime minister also held several bilateral conversations with world leaders and international organisations on the sidelines of the summit on Wednesday. Dozens of leaders are speaking during the “ high-level segment ” taking place on Wednesday and Thursday, including Erdogan, Iran’s President Masoud Pezeshkian and Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, whose country hosted last year’s climate talks. “Nature — no less than people — is also paying a heavy price for armed conflicts. The starkest example of this is Gaza… what has taken place in Gaza is not only a genocide, but it is also an ecocide,” Erdogan said to applause on Wednesday. The United States, the world’s largest historical emitter, has skipped the talks for the second year in a row after President Donald Trump — who has called global warming a hoax — withdrew the US from climate cooperation following his return to office in 2025. Negotiators from nearly 200 countries are seeking agreement on a plan to increase the share of electricity in global energy use and revive stalled efforts to move away from fossil fuels. On Wednesday, the UN chief told world leaders at the summit that the slow international response to climate change so far had placed the world on a path to destruction. Governments must fight harder to preserve the planet for future generations, he said, in comments that set the tone for two days of rapid-fire speeches by world leaders. “The brutal truth is that the climate crisis is outrunning us. This is the path to mutually assured destruction,” Guterres said, pointing to rising emissions, global temperatures and worsening climate-driven disasters. “But science is not telling us to surrender. It is telling us to fight harder.”
